label: Fused silica
name: Fused silica (Corning 7980, Heraeus Suprasil, Infrasil)
class_note: The low-nonlinearity reference glass: n₂ = 2.74×10⁻²⁰ m²/W at 1053 nm, no χ(2). Writing lowers n₂ inside the guide (Blömer 2006), yet long arrays still support discrete solitons (Szameit 2005).
trade_names: HPFS 7980 (Corning), Suprasil 1 / 2 (high-OH synthetic) (Heraeus), Suprasil 311 / 312 (synthetic, ~200 ppm OH for 311) (Heraeus), Suprasil 3001 / 3002 (low-OH synthetic, < 1 ppm) (Heraeus), Infrasil 301 (fused natural quartz, low OH) (Heraeus)
composition: Pure amorphous SiO₂. Grades differ in OH content: Suprasil 1/2 ≈ 1000 ppm, Suprasil 311 ≈ 200 ppm, Suprasil 3001/3002 < 1 ppm, Infrasil 301 ≤ 8 ppm.
index_change: Type I: a smooth positive Δn in the focus forms the core directly. At higher energy, Type II nanogratings make the track birefringent and scattering; useful for birefringent elements and selective etching, avoided for low-loss guides.
typical_delta_n: 6×10⁻⁴ – 1×10⁻³ at 100 kHz, 800 nm, NA 0.35 (Rechtsman 2013: 7×10⁻⁴). Up to 6.5×10⁻³ with heat accumulation (Appl. Phys. A 2015).
writing_regime: Established route at ≤ 100 kHz: the Szameit platform writes Corning 7980 with a RegA 9000 amplifier (800 nm, 130–150 fs, 100 kHz, 250–450 nJ, NA 0.35, ~100 mm/min). MHz heat accumulation also works, in a narrower window: at 1 MHz, low loss needed the 522 nm second harmonic instead of the 1045 nm fundamental (Shah 2005).
best_loss: 0.07 dB/cm with multiscan writing (Skryabin 2024); ~0.2 dB/cm for single-scan Szameit-group guides (Kremer 2019, Maczewsky 2017).
dlw_notes: Single-beam writing at NA 0.35 gives elliptical cross-sections (11 × 4 µm, Rechtsman 2013) and modes of 10.4 × 8.0 µm at 633 nm (Maczewsky 2017); multiscan gives square, fibre-matched modes. At 1 kHz, circular writing polarization gave up to twice the index contrast of linear (Little 2008).

our_laser: Inside our class: Imai 2017 wrote 0.2 dB/cm guides in fused silica with the 1030 nm fundamental of a 250 fs Yb solid-state laser at 150 kHz, NA 0.42 and slit shaping (energy and speed not retrieved), i.e. a low-rate, non-cumulative Type I (positive Δn) recipe the CARBIDE covers directly (150 kHz, ≥208 fs, slit). The MHz cumulative route is the main caveat at ~1 µm: Shah 2005 (IMRA fibre laser) could not make low-loss guides at the 1045 nm fundamental and wrote at 522 nm, 1 MHz instead, and the best multiscan result (Skryabin 2024, 0.07 dB/cm) used 515 nm, 270 fs, 1 MHz, 14–70 nJ, NA 0.55 — wavelengths our CARBIDE cannot make (no harmonic module).

class_note_full: Fused silica is the low-nonlinearity reference: n2 = (2.74 ± 0.17)×10⁻²⁰ m²/W at 1053 nm (Milam 1998), no χ(2) (centrosymmetric glass). In fs-written guides the effective n2 is lower than in bulk and depends on writing parameters (blomer2006nonlinear), yet still high enough for discrete solitons in long waveguide arrays (szameit2005discrete).
composition_full: Pure amorphous SiO2. Grades differ mainly in OH and metal-impurity content: Suprasil 3001/3002/300 OH < 1 ppm and total metals < 1 ppm (Heraeus datasheet); Suprasil 1/2 ~1000 ppm OH, Suprasil 311 ~200 ppm (arXiv cond-mat/0203284); Infrasil 301 (natural, dry) ≤ 8 ppm OH. Corning 7980 OH content not retrieved.
index_change_full: Type I: smooth, positive Δn in the focal volume that forms the guiding core directly (no depressed cladding needed). This is the regime of the Szameit-group lattices (Δn = 7×10⁻⁴ in rechtsman2013floquet) and of low-loss multiscan guides (skryabin2024multiscan); a 2021 PMC paper on Corning 7980 is explicitly titled 'Type I waveguide … in fused silica'. Mechanism linked to a change of Si–O ring structure / densification (little2008polarization title; davis1996writing also reports laser-induced defects). Type II: at higher pulse energy, self-organised nanogratings form; they make the modification birefringent and cause polarization-dependent scattering in waveguides (PMC9416729 title) — normally avoided for low-loss guides, but used for birefringent elements and selective etching. Type III: voids / micro-explosions at the highest intensities (definition from general literature; no source retrieved). Thresholds between the regimes were not retrieved.
typical_delta_n_full: ~6×10⁻⁴ – 1×10⁻³ for 100 kHz / 800 nm, NA 0.35 writing (rechtsman2013floquet: 7×10⁻⁴; queralto2020susy: ≈7×10⁻⁴; npj Nanophotonics 2024 review: 6×10⁻⁴–10⁻³). Heat-accumulation regime: 4×10⁻³ (non-thermal) → 6.5×10⁻³ (heat accumulation) in one Appl. Phys. A 2015 study (doi 10.1007/s00339-015-8990-x), with a negative-Δn surround. Circular writing polarization at 1 kHz gave up to 2× the index contrast of linear (little2008polarization). davis1996writing: 0.01–0.035 in pure and Ge-doped silica at high dose.
writing_regime_full: Two routes with different physics. (1) Established low-loss route, ~100 kHz and lower: Szameit/Nolte platform with a Coherent RegA 9000 Ti:sapphire amplifier, 800 nm, ~130–150 fs, 100 kHz, 250–450 nJ, NA 0.35, ~100 mm/min in Corning 7980 — maczewsky2017anomalous (150 fs, 450 nJ, depth 671–883 µm, 0.2 dB/cm, mode 10.4 × 8.0 µm at 633 nm), queralto2020susy (130 fs, 250 nJ, 91–103 mm/min, Δn ≈ 7×10⁻⁴), kremer2019pt (450 nJ, 0.2 dB/cm). little2008polarization made low-loss guides at 1 kHz. (2) MHz heat-accumulation route: possible in fused silica, but the retrieved sources show a narrower window than in borosilicates. shah2005waveguide (IMRA µJewel fibre laser) could not make low-loss guides at the 1045 nm fundamental and moved to the 522 nm second harmonic at 1 MHz; IMRA patent US 7684450 says the same (1045 nm: high loss; 522 nm: very low loss in fused silica). Eaton et al., Opt. Express 13, 4708 (2005) studied 0.1–5 MHz in fused silica and borosilicates, but its low-loss headline (~0.2 dB/cm at 1 MHz) is for Schott AF45 borosilicate, not silica; a thermal-diffusion model tracks the growth of the modified zone above 200 kHz. Eaton, Ng, Osellame et al., J. Non-Cryst. Solids 357, 2387 (2011) report (title) high index contrast in fused silica by combining tight focusing with a high repetition rate (abstract not retrieved). CORRECTION: a blanket statement that heat accumulation gives poor guides in fused silica is not supported by the retrieved sources. Appl. Phys. A (2015), doi 10.1007/s00339-015-8990-x: going from the non-thermal to the heat-accumulation regime raised the induced Δn in fused silica from 4×10⁻³ to 6.5×10⁻³ (aspect ratio 2.1 → <1.5), with a wide surrounding region of decreased index; the authors used it for a 0.3 dB/cm depressed-cladding (tubular) guide. Mechanism: silica belongs to the glasses with anomalous density behaviour versus fictive temperature (density rises with T_f; J. Am. Ceram. Soc. paper, Kyoto repository), fs-induced density changes in SiO2 have been analysed as a fictive-temperature effect (Bressel et al., Opt. Mater. Express 1, 605 (2011); abstract not retrieved), and in heat-accumulation writing the quench raises T_f by an amount that scales with the repetition rate (secondary: British Glass knowledge-base summary). No retrieved source states that silica's thermal diffusivity or high working point is the reason MHz guides are poorer; the first-pass paragraph marked 'our reasoning' stays unsourced and should be labelled as such or removed. For our CARBIDE (1025 nm): the only retrieved warning is shah2005waveguide / US 7684450 (MHz writing at the ~1 µm fundamental gave high loss in fused silica). The ≤100 kHz, ~1 µm case was not checked;
best_loss_full: 0.07 dB/cm, multiscan, skryabin2024multiscan (test wavelength not retrieved). The same 0.07 dB/cm is also reported in Opt. Lett. 47, 4766 (2022) ('Effectively writing low propagation and bend loss waveguides in the silica glass…', authors not verified). Typical Szameit-group single-scan guides: ~0.2 dB/cm (kremer2019pt).
dlw_notes_full: Wavelength check for our CARBIDE (1025 nm): the 0.07 dB/cm multiscan record (skryabin2024multiscan) was written at 515 nm, not at the Yb fundamental. The retrieved fused-silica result at the 1030 nm fundamental is imai2017yb1030 (150 kHz, 250 fs, NA 0.42, slit, 0.2 dB/cm). Hernandez-Rueda et al. (arXiv:1805.02191) report that thresholds, track size and the usable energy range depend strongly on writing wavelength.

label: EAGLE XG
name: Corning EAGLE XG (with EAGLE 2000 and 1737F results)
class_note: Passive, low-loss substrate for 3D circuits and the standard glass of integrated quantum and topological photonics. Penn State also uses its Kerr nonlinearity at high peak power for soliton experiments (Jürgensen 2023, Jörg 2025).
composition: Alkaline-earth boro-aluminosilicate (Corning).
index_change: Guides form by cumulative heating: the modified zone grows with repetition rate as a thermal-diffusion model predicts, with the melt radius set by the softening point (Eaton 2005, 2008).
writing_regime: Cumulative heating at 0.25–2 MHz. Heat accumulation starts near 900 nJ at 200 kHz but near 80 nJ at 2 MHz, and one window (~200 mW, ~15 mm/s) minimises insertion loss over 0.2–2 MHz (Eaton 2008). Recipes: Milan, 1030 nm, 300 fs, 1 MHz, 220 nJ, NA 0.6, 40 mm/s (Bentivegna 2015); Penn State, 1030 nm, 260 fs, 500 kHz, ~400 nJ, 8 mm/s (Jürgensen 2023).
dlw_notes: Thermal post-annealing removes the outer index ring and leaves single-mode, low-bend-loss guides (Arriola 2013). The writing polarization does not set the waveguide birefringence here; tilting the cross-section gives integrated waveplates (Corrielli 2014). Datasheet n = 1.510 at 589.3 nm.

class_note_full: Used as a passive, low-loss substrate for 3D waveguide circuits. The Rechtsman group also uses its optical Kerr nonlinearity at high peak power for soliton experiments (Jürgensen 2023, Jörg 2025). n2 value not retrieved.
composition_full: Alkaline earth boro-aluminosilicate (Corning PI sheet); wt% composition not given in the retrieved excerpt.
index_change_full: Guiding modification formed by cumulative heating: guide diameter grows with repetition rate and follows a thermal-diffusion model with the melt radius set by the softening point, 985 °C for EAGLE2000 (Eaton 2005, 2008). Sign/profile of Δn not retrieved.
typical_delta_n_full: not retrieved
writing_regime_full: Cumulative heating (MHz) works. Eaton 2008 (EAGLE2000, 1045 nm): smooth transition from diffusion-only transport at 200 kHz to strong heat accumulation at 0.5-2 MHz; starting heat accumulation needs ~900 nJ at 200 kHz but ~80 nJ at 2 MHz; one window (~200 mW, ~15 mm/s) minimises insertion loss across 0.2-2 MHz. Eaton 2005: heat accumulation above ~200 kHz; higher rep rate gives larger, lower-loss guides; AF45 and 1737F gave the smoothest, lowest-loss guides at 1045 nm. Penn State topological-photonics work in EAGLE XG uses 250-500 kHz: Coherent RegA 9000 at 800 nm, 270 fs, 250 kHz, 820 nJ, NA 0.55, cylindrical telescope (arXiv:2006.13242); Menlo BlueCut at 1030 nm, 260 fs, 500 kHz, ~400 nJ, 8 mm/s single pass (Jürgensen 2023).
best_loss_full: No EAGLE-specific loss value retrieved. Closest: ~0.2 dB/cm in Schott AF45 at 1 MHz (eaton2005heat), test wavelength not retrieved.
dlw_notes_full: Not covered: mode symmetry, thermal annealing (e.g. Arriola/Gross, Macquarie), birefringence/polarization-insensitive writing (Osellame/Corrielli, POLIMI), typical Δn. Datasheet n = 1.510 @ 589.3 nm (Corning 2023). The 1.473 @ 1550 nm quoted in arXiv:2006.13242 is 0.037 lower; treat it as unconfirmed. Milan writing recipe in EAGLE2000 (bentivegna2015scattershot): cavity-dumped Yb:KYW, 1030 nm, ~300 fs, 1 MHz, 220 nJ, NA 0.6, 40 mm/s; Penn State (jorg2025optical): BlueCut 1030 nm, 500 kHz, ~225 mW at focus, 8 mm/s; Chile (arXiv:2109.01756): BlueCut 1030 nm, 230 fs, 500 kHz, 20×, 0.4 mm/s. Thermal post-annealing to remove the outer index ring and get low-bend-loss single-mode guides: arriola2013lowbend (glass grade unconfirmed).

name: SCHOTT BOROFLOAT 33
writing_regime: An ion-trap chip used the 520 nm second harmonic of a 1040 nm laser at 1 MHz and 209 fs (Wahl 2026). Bragg-grating waveguide bundles were written with a low-rate fs laser (Thiel 2015).
dlw_notes: Used as the substrate of an ion-trap chip with integrated fs-written waveguides (Wahl 2026), and for Bragg-grating waveguide bundles together with fused silica and AF 32 eco (Thiel 2015).
our_laser: No waveguide recipe at the Yb fundamental was found: Wahl 2026 wrote its BF33 guides with the 520 nm second harmonic of a Spectra-Physics Spirit (1 MHz, 209 fs), which the CARBIDE cannot produce, and Thiel 2015 used a low-repetition-rate laser (rate not retrieved). The AIP commissioning study (arXiv 2026, laser not retrieved) found a negative-index (Type II) modification with crack-like features in Borofloat 33, so a 1025 nm attempt should expect negative Δn: plan a new rate/energy scan and consider double-line or depressed-cladding geometries.
open_questions: No propagation loss in dB/cm found yet.
index_change_full: Negative on-axis index change (Type II) with crack-like, non-uniform features in a substrate screen (aip2026commissioning; laser not retrieved). Wahl 2026 nevertheless wrote single-mode guides at 520 nm, 1 MHz, 209 fs, so the response depends on writing conditions.
dlw_notes_full: Two papers known: wahl2026iontrap (BF33 ion-trap waveguide) and thiel2015bgwbundles (Bragg grating waveguide bundles in BOROFLOAT 33). No loss value in dB/cm found for BOROFLOAT 33 (queries: 'femtosecond laser written waveguides Borofloat OR Pyrex borosilicate glass propagation loss dB/cm repetition rate'; 'BOROFLOAT 33 OR Borofloat33 femtosecond laser inscribed optical waveguide written inside glass').
open_questions_full: No fs-written waveguide paper collected for this glass.

label: AF 32 eco
name: SCHOTT AF 32 eco
composition: Alkali-free aluminoborosilicate thin glass, free of arsenic and antimony.
dlw_notes: Bragg-grating waveguide bundles written with a low-rate fs laser (Thiel 2015). A review of integrated quantum photonics (Corrielli, Crespi, Osellame, arXiv:2110.06162) names AF 32 among the most used substrates. Its predecessor AF45 gave ~0.2 dB/cm at 1 MHz (Eaton 2005).
dlw_sources:
https://www.schott.com/en-ie/products/af-32-eco-p1000308
https://www.pgo-online.com/intl/af32.html
https://arxiv.org/pdf/2110.06162 ; https://publica.fraunhofer.de/entities/publication/29a50214-33a7-4b3c-9c35-98608e13185f
first-pass paper entries (thiel2015bgwbundles, bentivegna2015scattershot, eaton2005heat)
our_laser: No paper with a laser in our class: Thiel 2015 wrote Bragg-grating waveguide bundles in AF 32 eco with a low-repetition-rate fs laser (rate and wavelength not retrieved). Closest in-class recipes are the ~1 MHz, 1030–1045 nm cumulative recipes in the related alkali-free glasses EAGLE (Bentivegna 2015) and AF45 (Eaton 2005); whether AF 32 eco gives positive Δn at 1025 nm needs a new energy/speed scan.
open_questions: A waveguide paper on AF 32 eco with full writing parameters and loss.
composition_full: Alkali-free aluminoborosilicate, made without arsenic and antimony; distributor notes up to 0.2 wt% alkali from raw-material traces. wt% composition not retrieved.
dlw_notes_full: Only one paper naming AF 32 eco was found (thiel2015bgwbundles, Bragg grating waveguide bundles; no AF 32 loss value in its abstract). The review arXiv:2110.06162 (Corrielli, Crespi, Osellame) names Schott AF32 among the most used substrates for integrated quantum photonics, but no specific AF32 waveguide paper with parameters was identified (queries: 'femtosecond laser written waveguides AF32 OR AF 32 OR AF32 eco Schott glass'; 'Schott AF32 borosilicate quantum photonic circuit pulse energy repetition rate'; 'AF32 glass femtosecond laser written waveguide array arXiv photonic lattice'). The closest well-characterised relative is SCHOTT AF45: ~0.2 dB/cm at 1 MHz (eaton2005heataccumulation).
open_questions_full: No fs-written waveguide paper collected for this glass.

label: D 263 T eco
name: SCHOTT D 263 T eco
composition: Clear borosilicate thin glass, free of added arsenic and antimony.
our_laser: No fs-written waveguide paper was found for D 263 T eco (none in the first pass, none in one search this pass). Closest: ~1 MHz, 1030–1047 nm cumulative recipes in the borosilicate crown BK7 (Chen 2018; Eaton 2008); D 263 is a different composition, so Δn sign, window and loss must be measured.
open_questions: No fs-written waveguide paper found in a targeted literature search (October 2026). Listed for its suppliers.
composition_full: Clear borosilicate glass with high chemical resistance, made without added arsenic and antimony refining agents. wt% composition not retrieved.
dlw_notes_full: No fs-written waveguide paper found in a targeted search (queries: 'femtosecond laser written waveguides D263 OR D 263 Schott borosilicate glass'; 'D263T OR D 263 T OR D263 T eco glass femtosecond laser inscribed waveguides OR laser written OR direct laser writing'; 'Schott D 263 thin glass femtosecond laser waveguide Bragg grating Fraunhofer OR point-by-point OR laser inscription').
open_questions_full: No fs-written waveguide paper collected for this glass.

label: Soda-lime / B 270
name: Soda-lime glass (float, SCHOTT B 270)
index_change: Positive Δn in the written track. A single scan with beam shaping guides; multiscan smooths the inhomogeneous modified volume and cuts scattering loss (Dyakonov 2016).
writing_regime: Slit beam shaping plus multiscan gave single-mode guides (Dyakonov 2016).
best_loss: 0.86 dB/cm at 800 nm in extra-white soda-lime glass (Dyakonov 2016)
dlw_notes: Among the first glasses written: Davis 1996 wrote index-increased lines in soda-lime silicate (paper listed under fused silica).
our_laser: Dyakonov 2016 reached 0.86 dB/cm (at 800 nm) in extra-white soda-lime glass with slit shaping plus multiscan, but its laser parameters were not retrieved, so it is not known whether the recipe is in our class. Both techniques are available with the CARBIDE; wavelength-, rate- and energy-specific settings need a new scan.
open_questions: Only one waveguide paper found; none for SCHOTT B 270 or microscope slides.
index_change_full: Positive Δn in the written track; a single scan with beam shaping can guide, and multiscan smooths the inhomogeneous modified volume to cut scattering loss (dyakonov2016sodalime).
best_loss_full: 0.86 dB/cm at 800 nm, extra-white soda-lime glass, slit shaping + multiscan (dyakonov2016sodalime)
dlw_notes_full: Only one fs-written waveguide paper found for soda-lime glass in a targeted search (queries: 'femtosecond laser written optical waveguides soda-lime glass propagation loss repetition rate pulse energy'; 'femtosecond laser waveguide inscription microscope slide soda lime silicate glass refractive index change guiding'; 'B270 OR B 270 glass femtosecond laser written waveguide'; 'soda-lime glass femtosecond laser waveguide high repetition rate heat accumulation'). No SCHOTT B 270 or microscope-slide waveguide paper found. Kyoto-group work on heat accumulation in soda-lime glass exists but concerns modification, not waveguides.
open_questions_full: No fs-written waveguide paper collected for this glass.

label: Gorilla Glass
name: Corning Gorilla Glass
index_change: Type I (positive Δn) guides for pulse durations from 250 fs to 15 ps. At higher pulse energy the guides become ring-mode and finally the core turns negative as alkali ions migrate outward (Lv 2020).
writing_regime: Guides written with 1 kHz fs pulses (Almeida 2018) and with 250 fs – 15 ps pulses (Lv 2020).
dlw_notes: Proposed for photonic devices written into smartphone cover glass (Lapointe 2014). Its third-order nonlinearity was measured in bulk and in written guides (Almeida 2018).
our_laser: Lv 2020 obtained Type I guides in Gorilla glass for pulse durations from 250 fs to 15 ps, a range the CARBIDE largely covers (208 fs–7.8 ps); higher pulse energy turned single-mode guides into ring-mode guides and finally a negative-Δn core from alkali migration. Wavelength, rate, energy and speed were not retrieved there (Lapointe 2014 none; Almeida 2018 used 1 kHz, reachable only by pulse picking), so start at low energy and use pulse duration as a scan parameter.
open_questions: No propagation loss in dB/cm found yet.
index_change_full: Type I (positive Δn) guides for pulse durations from 250 fs to 15 ps. At higher pulse energy the guides become ring-mode and finally the core shows a negative Δn, with alkali ions migrating outward at different rates (lv2020gorilla).
dlw_notes_full: No dB/cm loss value for Gorilla glass was retrieved. Also found but not entered (author list not seen): Proc. SPIE 10091, 1009109 (DOI 10.1117/12.2251182), 'Fabrication of waveguides in Gorilla Glass with fs pulses and …', using 120 fs pulses at 520, 650 and 775 nm and 1 kHz, guides ~15 mm long written 100 µm deep with 250 nJ–5 µJ, and self-phase modulation / white light from ~450 nm when 775 nm pulses are coupled in.
open_questions_full: No fs-written waveguide paper collected for this glass.

label: La–K phosphate
name: La–K phosphate glass
class_note: Madrid platform in which the index change comes from laser-driven ion migration.
composition: La₂O₃–K₂O–P₂O₅-type phosphate.
index_change: La and K cross-migrate under the laser; the La-rich zone forms a high-index core.
writing_regime: 500 kHz, NA 0.68. Below ~600 nJ the modified volume grows; at 610–730 nJ the energy mainly drives La–K cross-migration (Toney Fernandez 2015).
dlw_notes: In a La-free phosphate the index change is much smaller (Opt. Lett. 2013; not yet in the paper list).
our_laser: Fernandez 2015 wrote guides at 500 kHz with an NA 0.68 aspheric lens: below ~600 nJ light-element migration forms the guide, at 610–730 nJ heavy-element (La/K) cross-migration dominates — rate and energy are inside the CARBIDE's range (wavelength and pulse duration not retrieved). Expect a La-rich, high-index core made by ion migration (Fernandez 2013); caveat: migration changes the local composition, which matters if active ions are added.
open_questions: Laser wavelength and pulse duration of the 2015 study.
class_note_full: Included as the ion-migration (element redistribution) phosphate platform of the Madrid group; no property values retrieved.
composition_full: Phosphate glass with La and K (La–K cross-migration reported); exact composition and whether it is rare-earth doped NOT retrieved
index_change_full: Index change from fs-laser-driven La/K cross-migration (La-rich high-index core).
writing_regime_full: High rep. rate (500 kHz). Two regimes: regime I below ~600 nJ; for 610–730 nJ the pulse energy goes mainly into La–K cross-migration rather than into a larger modified volume.
dlw_notes_full: A 2013 Optics Letters paper on La-containing phosphate glass attributes the index change to ion migration and reports a much smaller index change in the La-free glass, caused by glass-structure rearrangement (search excerpt; paper details not verified).
open_questions_full:
Author list, DOI, laser wavelength/duration, and whether the glass is undoped or Er-doped must be checked (arXiv:1412.5783 full text).
No paper on Schott N-PK51 or other undoped commercial phosphates could be searched within the budget.

label: Er:Yb phosphate
name: Er:Yb phosphate laser glass (Kigre QX/Er, SCHOTT IOG-1)
class_note: Yb³⁺ absorbs the 980 nm pump and sensitises Er³⁺, which gives gain at 1.53–1.565 µm. Written guides gave 1.4 dB internal gain (2003), 1.2 dB net gain and lasing at 1533.5 nm (2004), and > 30 mW C-band lasers (2006).
trade_names: QX/Er (Er,Yb-codoped QX phosphate) (Kigre Inc.), IOG-1 (Er/Yb-doped, ion-exchangeable phosphate) (SCHOTT)
composition: Commercial Er³⁺/Yb³⁺ phosphate; base composition proprietary. Kigre QX at Macquarie: 2 % Er, 4 % Yb (Marshall 2008).
index_change: The sign depends on composition. Many phosphates give negative Δn; a zinc phosphate with O/P = 3.25 gives up to +5×10⁻⁴ (Fletcher 2011). The commercial Er:Yb phosphates in these papers gave guiding cores directly.
writing_regime: Both regimes work: 1 kHz amplified Ti:sapphire with slit shaping (Marshall 2008), and cavity-dumped oscillators at 166 kHz (270 nJ, Osellame 2004; 520 nm, 300 fs, Taccheo 2004) or 885 kHz (1040 nm, 350 fs, 250 nJ, Della Valle 2006). The 885 kHz, 1040 nm recipe is closest to our CARBIDE.
best_loss: ≈ 0.25 dB/cm, single-mode at 1.5 µm (Osellame 2003); < 0.4 dB/cm (Osellame 2006)
dlw_notes: Astigmatic (Osellame 2003) or slit (Marshall 2008) beam shaping gives circular, fibre-matched modes, with coupling loss to SMF down to 0.1 dB per facet (Osellame 2006). DFB gratings can be written in the same pass as the guide (Marshall 2008).
our_laser: Directly in class: Della Valle 2005 wrote a C-band amplifier (9.2 dB peak internal gain at 1535 nm) with a cavity-dumped Yb:KYW oscillator at 1040 nm, 350 fs, 885 kHz, and the same kind of source at ~250 nJ and 0.05–0.1 mm/s gave a >50 mW waveguide laser (Della Valle 2006, values from an SPIE Newsroom summary); Osellame 2004 used 270 nJ at 166 kHz. Expect a directly guiding core in commercial Er:Yb phosphate; caveat: these speeds are very slow and the sign of Δn in phosphates depends on composition, so test each new glass.
open_questions:
Datasheet values for QX/Er and IOG-1 (n at 1 µm, thermal conductivity).
Whether SCHOTT still sells IOG-1.
class_note_full: Yb3+ absorbs the ~980 nm pump and sensitises Er3+, which gives gain in the 1.53-1.565 um telecom band. fs-written waveguides gave 1.4 dB internal gain (2003), 1.2 dB net gain (2004), lasing at 1533.5 nm (2004) and >30 mW C-band lasers (2006).
composition_full: Commercial Er3+/Yb3+-codoped phosphate; base composition proprietary and not retrieved. Kigre QX used by Macquarie (marshall2008dfb): 2 % Er / 4 % Yb (basis not stated in retrieved excerpt).
index_change_full: Sign of fs-induced delta-n in phosphates depends on composition. Krol (NSF DMR-1207520 abstract): phosphate glasses typically give negative delta-n in laser-exposed regions, which hurts device performance, while certain compositions give positive changes. Fletcher et al., Opt. Express 19(9), 7929-7936 (2011): a zinc polyphosphate with O/P = 3.25 gives positive delta-n in the focal volume above threshold; of five compositions tested only 60ZnO-40P2O5 (O/P = 3.25) worked well, delta-n up to +5e-4. Companion Fletcher et al. J. Appl. Phys. paper on Er-Yb-doped zinc phosphate: waveguide quality depends very strongly on small composition changes; good guides need O/P = 3.25. Commercial Er:Yb phosphates (Kigre QX; Polimi's Er:Yb phosphate) did give directly guiding cores in the papers listed here, so 'phosphate = negative delta-n' is not universal. Test a new phosphate before assuming either sign.
typical_delta_n_full: not reported in the retrieved abstracts
writing_regime_full: Both regimes worked: kHz amplified pulses (1 kHz, 120 fs, 800 nm, slit; marshall2008dfb) and 166 kHz cavity-dumped oscillators (270 nJ at 166 kHz, osellame2004oscillator; 520 nm, 300 fs, 166 kHz, taccheo2004laser). A Polimi repository abstract of Della Valle et al. 2005 (venue not confirmed) reports writing with 1040 nm, 350 fs, 885 kHz pulses from a cavity-dumped Yb:KYW oscillator, giving 9.2 dB peak internal gain at 1535 nm. That regime is closest to our CARBIDE (1025 nm, 60-1008 kHz).
best_loss_full: < 0.4 dB/cm (osellame2006jstqe, abstract; 1.5 um region implied, wavelength not stated) — vs ~0.25 dB/cm in osellame2003astigmatic (abstract)
dlw_notes_full: Beam shaping (astigmatic: osellame2003astigmatic; slit: marshall2008dfb) was used to get circular, fibre-matched modes; coupling loss to SMF as low as 0.1 dB/facet (osellame2006jstqe). Gratings for DFB lasers can be written in the same pass as the waveguide (marshall2008dfb). Ion-migration studies in Er-doped phosphates (Madrid group) were not verified.
open_questions_full:
No Crossref check was possible (api.crossref.org, doi.org and publisher sites blocked by the session proxy; WebFetch failed on every host). DOIs come from web-search listings or the Optica DOI pattern and need a Crossref check.
Datasheet properties not retrieved (search budget used up): refractive index at ~1 um and 1.5 um, Tg, CTE, thermal conductivity, phonon energy, absorption/emission cross-sections, exact Er/Yb concentrations for Kigre QX/Er, Schott IOG-1 and Kigre MM-2. Whether 'MM2' is a Kigre product was not verified.
Della Valle et al. 2005, 'C-band waveguide amplifier produced by femtosecond laser writing' (Polimi repository; abstract: Yb:KYW oscillator, 1040 nm, 885 kHz, 350 fs, 9.2 dB peak internal gain at 1535 nm, 5.2 dB at 1565 nm, 1.9 dB insertion loss). Real (repository record), but journal/DOI not confirmed (likely Opt. Express 2005); left out of papers.
Della Valle, Taccheo, Osellame, Festa, Cerullo, Laporta 2007, '1.5 um single longitudinal mode waveguide laser fabricated by femtosecond laser writing' (Polimi repository; abstract: >50 mW single-longitudinal-mode output, 21 % slope efficiency, Er:Yb phosphate, cavity-dumped oscillator). Journal/DOI not confirmed (likely Opt. Express 2007); left out of papers.
Not checked at all: Osellame et al. 2005 Opt. Express '26 MHz stretched-cavity Ti:sapphire' writing study; Chan, Huser, Risbud, Hayden, Krol 2003 APL on IOG-1 phosphate; Fletcher et al. (Krol group) zinc-phosphate composition and RE-doping studies; Fernandez/Solis (Madrid) ion-migration waveguides and del Hoyo et al. amplifiers/lasers; Psaila/Thomson/Kar Er:Yb oxyfluoride-silicate waveguide amplifier and laser (2007-2008).
Host of osellame2003astigmatic: the retrieved abstract says only 'Er:Yb-doped glass'; that it is phosphate (and which commercial glass) is not confirmed.

label: Yb phosphate
name: Yb phosphate laser glass (Kigre QX/Yb)
class_note: Yb³⁺ (pump ~976 nm, emission ~1030 nm) has a small quantum defect. A written DFB laser reached 102 mW at 1033 nm with < 2 pm linewidth (Ams 2009).
trade_names: QX/Yb (Yb-doped QX phosphate) (Kigre Inc.), IOG-1 (Yb-doped, ion-exchangeable phosphate) (SCHOTT)
composition: Kigre QX phosphate with 9 wt% Yb (Ams 2009).
index_change: Waveguides and Bragg gratings are written directly in the glass (Ams 2009, 2012).
dlw_notes: A Macquarie comparison of Yb silicate and Yb phosphate waveguide lasers found similar power and threshold. The GHz mode-locked Yb:IOG-1 lasers from St Andrews/Southampton used ion-exchanged, not laser-written, guides.
our_laser: No Yb-phosphate paper with writing parameters in our class was retrieved (Ams 2009 and 2012, Macquarie QX/Yb DFB lasers, parameters not retrieved). Closest: the 1040 nm, 350 fs, 885 kHz cavity-dumped Yb:KYW recipe that made amplifiers and lasers in Yb-codoped Er:Yb phosphate (Della Valle 2005, 2006); a new energy/speed scan is needed, and (our reasoning, not from a paper) 1025 nm lies closer to the Yb3+ absorption than 1040 nm, so check for linear absorption by the writing beam.
open_questions: Writing parameters of the Ams papers.
class_note_full: Yb3+ two-level system (pump ~976 nm, emission ~1030 nm) with small quantum defect. fs-written DFB lasers in Yb phosphate reached 102 mW at 1033 nm with < 2 pm linewidth (ams2009yb100mw).
composition_full: Commercial Yb3+-doped phosphate; base composition proprietary and not retrieved. Kigre QX doped with 9 wt% Yb (ams2009yb100mw); 12 wt% Yb-doped IOG-1 used by Southampton for ion-exchanged (not fs-written) waveguides.
index_change_full: Guiding waveguides plus Bragg gratings written directly in Yb-doped QX phosphate (ams2009yb100mw, ams2012dualwavelength); sign and size of delta-n not given in the retrieved abstracts. A Macquarie OECC/ACOFT 2014 comparison of fs-written Yb silicate and Yb phosphate waveguide lasers found similar output power and threshold, but says the mechanism of the index change can affect long-term laser performance.
typical_delta_n_full: not reported in the retrieved abstracts
writing_regime_full: Not retrieved for the Yb papers. The same group's Er:Yb QX work used 1 kHz, 120 fs, 800 nm Ti:sapphire with slit shaping (marshall2008dfb, secondary excerpt).
best_loss_full: not retrieved
dlw_notes_full: The GHz mode-locked Yb:phosphate waveguide lasers from St Andrews/Southampton (Choudhary et al., Opt. Lett. 37, 4416 (2012), DOI 10.1364/OL.37.004416; Lagatsky et al., Opt. Express 21, 19608 (2013), DOI 10.1364/OE.21.019608, up to 15.2 GHz) used ion-exchanged Yb:IOG-1 channels per the Southampton repository text, not fs-written ones, so they are not listed as papers. fs-written mode-locked Yb lasers retrieved here are in bismuthate (see that entry).
open_questions_full:
No Crossref check was possible (proxy blocked); DOIs follow the Optica pattern and need checking.
Writing parameters (rep rate, energy, NA, speed) for ams2009yb100mw and ams2012dualwavelength not retrieved.
Datasheet properties (n, Tg, CTE, thermal conductivity, phonon energy, cross-sections) for Kigre QX/Yb and Schott IOG-1 not retrieved.
Yb silicate: only the Macquarie OECC/ACOFT 2014 conference record 'Comparison study of femtosecond direct-written monolithic waveguide lasers in Yb-doped silicate and phosphate glass' (IEEE, pp. 893-895) was found; authors, DOI and glass names not retrieved, so no Yb-silicate entry was made.
Other leads not verified: a fs-written Yb DBR phosphate waveguide laser with 31 % slope efficiency and 81 mW (source paper not identified); NWPU 'Experimental study of femtosecond laser written waveguide in Yb3+:phosphate glass and waveguide laser' (Acta Optica Sinica 34(4), 432003 (2014), authors not retrieved).

label: Nd phosphate
name: Nd phosphate laser glass (SCHOTT LG-760, Kigre)
class_note: Four-level Nd³⁺ ion lasing near 1.05 µm. Written guides keep the Nd³⁺ fluorescence (Long 2013), but no laser-written Nd phosphate waveguide laser was found.
index_change: Guiding comes from stress next to or inside written structures, not from a positive-Δn core: a double-line guide (Long 2013) and a cylindrical shell with a densified centre at 1 kHz, 120 fs (Dong 2013).
writing_regime: 1 kHz, 120 fs amplified pulses (Dong 2013).
best_loss: 1.2 dB/cm at 980 nm, double-line guide (Long 2013)
our_laser: No paper in our class: the retrieved Nd-phosphate guides are stress-guided, either double-line (Long 2013, laser not retrieved; 1.2 dB/cm at 980 nm) or a tubular shell written at 1 kHz, 120 fs, 90 µJ (Dong 2013) — 1 kHz needs pulse picking and 90 µJ is above our 85 µJ. Closest in-class route is the 885 kHz cavity-dumped Yb recipe from Er:Yb phosphate (Della Valle 2005); energy, speed and Δn sign need a new scan.
open_questions: A waveguide laser in Nd phosphate.
class_note_full: Nd3+ four-level laser ion (4F3/2 -> 4I11/2, ~1.05 um in phosphate hosts). No fs-written Nd-phosphate waveguide laser was found; the only retrieved fs-writing paper reports passive guiding and preserved Nd3+ fluorescence.
composition_full: Not retrieved (glass used in long2013ndphosphate not identified in the retrieved abstract).
index_change_full: In both papers found, guiding comes from stress next to or inside written structures, not from a positive-Δn track used as core: double-line guide between two tracks (long2013ndphosphate) and a cylindrical shell with a densified centre and rarefied outer region at 1 kHz, 120 fs (dong2013ndphosphate).
typical_delta_n_full: not reported in the retrieved abstract
writing_regime_full: not retrieved
best_loss_full: 1.2 dB/cm at 980 nm, double-line buried guide, scattering method (long2013ndphosphate, abstract)
dlw_notes_full: No fs-written waveguide LASER in Nd-doped phosphate glass was found in a targeted search (queries: 'femtosecond laser written waveguide laser Nd-doped phosphate glass 1054 nm lasing'; 'waveguide laser Nd-doped phosphate glass femtosecond direct writing LG-760 / Kigre / Nd:phosphate depressed cladding laser output'). Nd³⁺ fluorescence is preserved in the written guides (long2013ndphosphate). The closest active results found are in other phosphate compositions (Er/Yb phosphate, Yb phosphate), not Nd.
open_questions_full:
No fs-written Nd:phosphate waveguide LASER was found (search budget used up). Florea and Winick, J. Lightwave Technol. 2003 (fs-written devices incl. rare-earth-doped amplifiers) and Sikorski et al., Electron. Lett. 2000 (Nd-doped glass amplifier) were not confirmed; their Nd host (phosphate vs silicate) is unknown.
SCHOTT LG-760 / Kigre Nd-phosphate datasheet values (n, Tg, CTE, thermal conductivity, Nd concentration, emission peak, cross-section) not retrieved; Kigre product designation not verified.
long2013ndphosphate: writing laser parameters, loss value and first-author initials not retrieved.
Salamanca/Madrid group: cladding waveguides in Nd-doped wollastonite-tricalcium phosphate glass (120 fs, 1 kHz Ti:sapphire) found as a repository record only (gredos.usal.es); citation not confirmed.

label: Zinc tellurite (TZN)
name: Zinc tellurite glasses (TeO₂–ZnO, TZN)
class_note: High-index heavy-metal-oxide glasses for χ(3) photonics, transmitting into the mid-IR.
composition: TeO₂–ZnO (da Silva 2018); P/Na/Zn tellurite (Fernandez 2014); La-doped TeO₂–ZnO (Clabel Huamán 2025); Er-doped tellurite (Nandi 2006).
index_change: Depends on composition. With Na present, Te migrates into the focus (positive core) and Na moves out (Fernandez 2014). In TeO₂–ZnO the focus has negative Δn and light guides between two written lines (da Silva 2018).
writing_regime: Reported: 4 kHz, 80 fs (da Silva 2018); amplified Ti:sapphire, 45 fs (Nandi 2006).
best_loss: < 2.0 dB/cm internal (da Silva 2018)
our_laser: In class by laser type: Fernandez 2008 wrote active Er phospho-tellurite waveguides with internal gain across 1530–1610 nm using a compact cavity-dumped Yb oscillator (rate, energy and speed not retrieved). Other tellurite recipes are outside our class (Nandi 2006: 45 fs Ti:sapphire; da Silva 2018: 80 fs, 4 kHz, double line with negative Δn at the focus); caveat: Te/Na ion migration sets the index profile (Fernandez 2014) and the Δn sign depends on composition.
open_questions:
Datasheet n, n₂ and Tg.
Writing parameters of Fernandez 2014.
class_note_full: Tellurites are high-index heavy-metal-oxide glasses used for χ(3) photonics; no n, n2 or transmission value could be retrieved from a datasheet or paper, so none are given here.
composition_full: Varies by paper: TeO2–ZnO (da Silva 2018); tellurite containing P, Na and Zn oxides (Fernandez 2014); La3+-doped tellurium–zinc glasses TZL5/TZL9 (Clabel Huamán 2025); Er-doped tellurite (Nandi 2006). Exact mol% not retrieved.
index_change_full: Composition-dependent. Fernandez 2014: Te migrates into the irradiated zone giving a positive-Δn core, Na cross-migrates to the Te-deficient zone giving a lower-index region; Raman shows more TeO3 and fewer TeO4 units in Te-rich zones (densification). Nandi 2006: migration of atoms toward the waveguide periphery causes the index change. da Silva 2018 (TeO2–ZnO): negative Δn at the focus, guiding between two written lines (double-line). Clabel Huamán 2025: irradiation converts TeO3 to TeO4 units; loss lower in TeO4-rich regions.
typical_delta_n_full: ~1e-4 at 632 nm for double-line guides in TeO2–ZnO (dasilva2018doubleline)
writing_regime_full: Not established from verified sources. Only stated rates: 4 kHz, 80 fs (dasilva2018doubleline); amplified Ti:sapphire 45 fs, rep. rate not stated (nandi2006tellurite).
best_loss_full: <2.0 dB/cm (internal loss, wavelength not stated in abstract; dasilva2018doubleline)
dlw_notes_full: Ion migration (Te vs Na) is the reported index mechanism in Na-containing tellurite; this is the same element-redistribution physics the Madrid (Solis) group reports for phosphates.
open_questions_full:
No property values (n, transmission, n2, Tg, density, CTE) could be sourced; datasheet/paper lookup still needed.
Laser parameters for fernandez2014ionmigration and clabelhuaman2025lanthanum need the full texts (Optics Express OA; PMC12163806).
Nandi 2006 glass is Er-doped; whether it is TZN-type not confirmed. Wavelength and rep. rate not in abstract.
Related but not included (active, Er-doped): Fernandez et al., 'Active waveguides written by femtosecond laser irradiation in an erbium-doped phospho-tellurite glass', Opt. Express 16(19) (2008) — title/journal seen in search only.
IPEN conference: 'Production and characterization of Femtosecond laser-written waveguides in a tellurium-zinc glass' (SEMINATEC 2016) — conference only, not included.

label: Tungsten tellurite
name: Tungsten tellurite glass (70TeO₂–22WO₃–8Bi₂O₃)
class_note: High-purity, low-OH tellurite used for supercontinuum generation around 2 µm in written waveguides.
composition: 70TeO₂–22WO₃–8Bi₂O₃ (mol%), high purity, low OH.
index_change: Depressed cladding: the written tracks form a low-index cladding around an unmodified core (Okhrimchuk 2018, 2020).
writing_regime: 1030 nm fs pulses through an NA 0.85 objective (Okhrimchuk 2018).
dlw_notes: Large-mode single-mode guides: mode-field diameter 12 µm (2018); 20 µm and single-mode over 1700–2100 nm with a 36-track cladding (2020).
our_laser: Partly in class: Okhrimchuk 2018 and 2020 wrote depressed-cladding single-mode guides (MFD 12 µm; 20 µm near 2 µm) with a 1030 nm fs laser through an NA 0.85 objective — the wavelength matches our CARBIDE, but rate, pulse duration, energy and speed were not retrieved. The written tracks act as low-index cladding, so plan a depressed-cladding geometry rather than a Type I core, with a new energy/rate scan.
open_questions: Repetition rate, pulse energy and loss.
class_note_full: Used for supercontinuum generation around 2 µm in fs-written depressed-cladding waveguides; numerical n2 not retrieved.
composition_full: 70TeO2–22WO3–8Bi2O3 (mol%), high purity, low OH content
index_change_full: Written as depressed-cladding (tracks around an unmodified core): the cladding tracks are used as the low-index region (Okhrimchuk 2018, 2020).
writing_regime_full: 1030 nm fs writing; rep. rate not retrieved.
dlw_notes_full: Large-mode-area single-mode guides: MFD 12 µm (okhrimchuk2018nonlinear), MFD 20 µm single-mode 1700–2100 nm with a 36-track cladding (okhrimchuk2020supercontinuum).
open_questions_full:
DOI of okhrimchuk2018nonlinear not seen in any source (Optica pattern would suggest 10.1364/OME.8.003424 — NOT verified).
Rep. rate, pulse duration, energy and losses of both papers need the full texts.
Not included (authors/journal not confirmed): 'Femtosecond laser writing of a depressed cladding single mode channel waveguide in high-purity tellurite glass', J. Non-Cryst. Solids (ScienceDirect pii S0022309317305902).
Not included (conference, authors not confirmed): 'Mid-IR Supercontinuum Generation in The Waveguide Inscribed in A Tellurite Glass', BGPPM 2018, JTh4A.8 (SC 1800–2200 nm, pump 1900 nm, 14 mm guide in tungstate-tellurite).
A search summary mentioned an octave-spanning SC (1.5–3.4 µm, 2.2 µm pump, 260 fs) in a depressed-cladding guide in the same glass; the paper could not be identified.

label: Lead germanate
name: Lead germanate glasses (GeO₂–PbO)
class_note: Heavy-metal germanate with high n₂; strong self-focusing during writing produces non-uniform structures that add loss.
composition: GeO₂–PbO (da Silva 2018); Yb-doped lead germanate GPGN (Khalid 2021).
index_change: GeO₂–PbO: negative Δn in the focus, so guides are double-line (da Silva 2018). GPGN: guides written both athermally (100 kHz) and with heat accumulation (1–5 MHz); Δn grows with repetition rate (Khalid 2021).
writing_regime: Both regimes work; the lowest loss came at 1 MHz (Khalid 2021).
best_loss: 0.2 dB/cm, written at 1 MHz (Khalid 2021)
our_laser: Closest: Khalid 2021 wrote guides in Yb-doped lead germanate at 100 kHz (athermal, Δn ~1e-4), 1 MHz and 5 MHz (thermal, up to ~5e-4); the 1 MHz guide had ~0.2 dB/cm and lased with up to ~28 % slope efficiency. 100 kHz and 1 MHz are within the CARBIDE's range, but wavelength, pulse duration, energy and NA were not retrieved, and the small Δn means weak confinement.
open_questions: Laser and objective used by Khalid 2021.
class_note_full: Heavy-metal-oxide germanate with high n2 (self-focusing during writing reported). Mostly used as a near/mid-IR laser host in DLW work so far; numerical n2/transmission not retrieved.
composition_full: GeO2–PbO (da Silva 2018); rare-earth (Yb3+)-doped lead-germanate 'GPGN' (Khalid 2021). mol% not retrieved.
index_change_full: GeO2–PbO (da Silva 2018): negative Δn at focus → double-line guides. GPGN (Khalid 2021): guiding written in athermal (100 kHz) and thermal (1, 5 MHz) regimes; Δn grows with rep. rate.
typical_delta_n_full: ~1e-4 (100 kHz) to ~5e-4 (5 MHz) (khalid2021leadgermanate); ~1e-4 at 632 nm, double line (dasilva2018doubleline)
writing_regime_full: Both athermal (100 kHz) and cumulative-heating (1–5 MHz) work; lowest loss at 1 MHz (khalid2021leadgermanate).
best_loss_full: 0.2 dB/cm (1 MHz written; khalid2021leadgermanate; the related SPIE abstract states 1550 nm)
dlw_notes_full: Strong self-focusing from the high n2 gives non-uniform guiding structures that add loss (SPIE 13440 abstract).
open_questions_full:
Writing laser system, wavelength, energy, NA and speed of khalid2021leadgermanate need the PMC full text (PMC8144420, open access).
Not included (authors not confirmed): SPIE Proc. 13440, 134400E (2024), 'Optimization of femtosecond laser-written waveguides in germanate glass for …', doi 10.1117/12.3055269 — GPGN, 0.2 dB/cm at 1550 nm, 27% slope (likely a conference version of Khalid 2021).
Not included (authors not retrieved): review 'Towards Integrated Photonics: a review of femtosecond laser-written double-line waveguides in GeO2-PbO glasses', Opt. Mater. (2026), ScienceDirect pii S0925346726001734.
Not included: 'S-Bend and Y Waveguide Architectures in Germanate Glasses Irradiated by Femtosecond Laser' (PMC11857262) — details not retrieved.
χ(2) lead: Lotarev et al., Crystals (Feb 2021), fs direct writing of crystalline lines in lead germanate glass close to Pb5Ge3O11 — title/DOI not retrieved.
No Heriot-Watt (Kar) lead-germanate DLW paper was found in the searches that could be run.

class_note: Mid-IR germanate; written guides demonstrated at 3.2 µm.
index_change: Type I positive Δn; multiscan writing shapes circular mid-IR modes (Tryoen 2026).
best_loss: 0.5 ± 0.1 dB/cm at 3.2 µm (Tryoen 2026)
our_laser: Tryoen 2026 made multiscan Type I guides in Corning 9754 (peak Δn 1.2e-2 at 600 nm, 0.5 dB/cm at 3.2 µm), but its writing parameters were not retrieved, so it is unknown whether the recipe is in our class. Multiscan is possible with the CARBIDE; the closest in-class germanate recipe is BGG at 1030 nm, 380 fs, 250 kHz, 500 nJ (Le Camus 2021), so a new scan is needed.
open_questions: Writing parameters and composition.
class_note_full: Mid-IR transmitting germanate; laser-written guides demonstrated at 3.2 µm. Property values not retrieved.
composition_full: Germanate-based heavy-oxide glass; composition not retrieved
index_change_full: Type I positive Δn (peak contrast 1.2e-2 at 600 nm) usable as guiding core; multiscan used to shape circular mid-IR modes.
typical_delta_n_full: (1.2 ± 0.07)e-2 peak at 600 nm (tryoen2026germanate)
writing_regime_full: Not retrieved.
best_loss_full: 0.5 ± 0.1 dB/cm at 3.2 µm (tryoen2026germanate)
dlw_notes_full: Multiscan writing; FDTD simulations based on measured index profiles.
open_questions_full:
Author list, group and laser parameters of tryoen2026germanate not retrieved.
Not included: 'Processing Maps and Nano-IR Diagnostics of Type I Modifications in Mid-IR Germanate-Based Optical Glass', Photonics 13(2), 197 (MDPI) — Type I writing in Corning 9754, index variation ~1.35e-2 to 2e-2; authors not retrieved.

label: Sodium germanate
name: Sodium germanate glass (22Na₂O·78GeO₂)
class_note: Modification study in the 50 kHz – 1 MHz range, which overlaps our laser; no waveguides yet.
composition: 22Na₂O·78GeO₂ (mol%).
index_change: At low repetition rate, nanogratings (form birefringence); at higher rate, Na₂Ge₄O₉ microcrystals around the track.
writing_regime: Retardance appears between ~70 and 200 kHz, depending on pulse energy (Lotarev 2023).
our_laser: Lotarev 2023 used nearly our laser class (Light Conversion PHAROS SP, 1030 nm, 1.2 ps, 67 kHz–1 MHz, 120 and 210 nJ, NA 0.65, static dots 50 µm deep): below a ~70–200 kHz threshold (lower at higher energy) birefringent nanogratings grow, above it cumulative heating crystallises Na2Ge4O9 around the spot. No waveguides were made; caveat: in our MHz regime this glass crystallises instead of giving a smooth Type I core, so guides need a new study (the low-rate nanograting regime suits birefringent elements).
open_questions: Wavelength, pulse duration and NA.
class_note_full: Included for its DLW-regime data in the 50 kHz–1 MHz range (overlaps the CARBIDE range); no waveguide paper found.
composition_full: 22Na2O·78GeO2 (mol%)
index_change_full: Low rep. rate: nanogratings (form birefringence). Higher rep. rate: peripheral microcrystallization of Na2Ge4O9.
writing_regime_full: PHAROS SP, 1030 nm, 1.2 ps, 120/210 nJ, NA 0.65, 67 kHz–1 MHz (lotarev2023sodiumgermanate): nanogratings (form birefringence) below a ~70–200 kHz threshold that falls with pulse energy; Na2Ge4O9 peripheral microcrystallization by cumulative heating above it.
dlw_notes_full: Modification study, not waveguides.
open_questions_full: Laser wavelength, pulse duration, energies and NA need the open-access full text (PMC10097084).

label: Barium gallo-germanate
name: Barium gallo-germanate glass (BGG)
class_note: Robust oxide glass transmitting to ~5 µm. Unlike fluorides and chalcogenides, it gives a positive Type I Δn of up to ~10⁻².
composition: Ga₂O₃–BaO–GeO₂.
index_change: Type I positive Δn over a wide range of conditions; the core is written directly.
typical_delta_n: 5–8×10⁻³ at 0.3–0.6 µJ and 250 kHz; up to ~10⁻² (Bérubé 2017)
writing_regime: 250 kHz works at 795 nm / 70 fs (Bérubé 2017) and at 1030 nm / 380 fs / 500 nJ (Le Camus 2021).
dlw_notes: Waveguide diameter tunable from 4 to 35 µm (Bérubé 2017). Mid-IR directional couplers at 2.85 µm (Le Camus 2021). A Tm-doped BGG single-scan waveguide laser has been reported (Dupont 2025).
our_laser: In class: Le Camus 2021 wrote mid-IR directional couplers in BGG (99 % cross transmission at 2.85 µm) at 1030 nm, 380 fs, 250 kHz, 500 nJ — directly reproducible with the CARBIDE. Bérubé 2017 shows Type I positive Δn up to ~1e-2 over a wide window at 250 kHz (795 nm, 70 fs Ti:sapphire, NA 0.55; 8e-3 at 0.3 µJ and 5 mm/s); caveat: NA and speed of the 1030 nm recipe and loss values were not retrieved.
open_questions:
Propagation loss.
Datasheet n, n₂ and Tg.
class_note_full: Robust oxide glass transmitting into the mid-IR (to ~5 µm), giving a positive Type I Δn up to ~1e-2 under fs writing, unlike fluorides/chalcogenides that often need depressed claddings.
composition_full: Ga2O3–BaO–GeO2; exact mol% not retrieved
index_change_full: Type I positive Δn in focus over a wide range of exposure conditions; guiding core directly.
typical_delta_n_full: 5e-3 – 8e-3 (0.3–0.6 µJ at 250 kHz), up to ~1e-2 (berube2017bgg)
writing_regime_full: 250 kHz (cumulative regime at moderate speeds) worked at 795 nm / 70 fs and at 1030 nm / 380 fs.
dlw_notes_full: Controllable waveguide diameter 4–35 µm (berube2017bgg). Directional couplers compared against identical structures in silica (lecamus2021couplers).
open_questions_full:
berube2017bgg: DOI not seen (Optica pattern would suggest 10.1364/OME.7.003124 — NOT verified); co-author list not retrieved; propagation loss not retrieved.
Conference version not included: SPIE Proc. 10522, 105220N, doi 10.1117/12.2290789 (title begins 'Femtosecond laser direct inscription of mid-IR transmitting waveguides in…').
Active, not included: Dupont et al., 'Lasing in a femtosecond-laser-written single-scan waveguide fabricated in Tm-doped BGG glass', Opt. Lett. 50(2), 666 (2025) — authors beyond first not retrieved.
Not included: HAL hal-03722136, 'Formation of nanogratings driven by ultrafast laser irradiation in mid-IR heavy oxide glasses' (BGG nanogratings).
A search summary cited a BGG (Ga2O3–BaO–GeO2) study with an 8.2 cm guide and <0.3 dB/cm at 1550 nm (ResearchGate 371585992, 'Investigation of Ga2O3-BaO-GeO2 glasses for ultrafast laser inscription'); bibliographic data could not be confirmed.
BGG density, Tg, CTE, n and n2 not retrieved.

label: Er/Yb bismuthate
name: Er- or Yb-doped bismuthate glass (Asahi Glass)
class_note: High-index host (n = 2.03) for Er³⁺ (1.53–1.56 µm) and Yb³⁺ (~1.04 µm). Written guides gave 2.3 dB/cm internal and 16 dB net gain (Er), and lasers with > 78 % slope efficiency (Yb).
composition: Bi₂O₃-based oxide doped with Er³⁺ or Yb³⁺; 1.6×10²⁶ m⁻³ Yb³⁺ in Mary 2013.
index_change: Positive Δn in the focus forms the core; multiscan writing gives symmetric, low-loss guides (Mary 2013).
writing_regime: MHz multiscan at low energy: 1047 nm, 350 fs, 1 MHz, ~50 nJ, NA 0.4, 200 µm deep (Mary 2013). Close to our CARBIDE's range.
best_loss: 4.0 dB fibre-to-fibre insertion loss for an 87 mm guide at 1618 nm (Thomson 2010)
dlw_notes: Er clustering limited the gain in one glass composition. Yb bismuthate guides also gave a 1.94 GHz mode-locked laser with 1.1 ps pulses.
dlw_sources:
https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.3401
https://doi.org/10.1364/OE.18.013212
https://www.ros.hw.ac.uk/handle/10399/2325
https://opg.optica.org/abstract.cfm?URI=ASSL-2015-AM5A.22
first-pass paper entries (mary2013graphene, beecher2010nanotube, mary2012ybbismuthate, thomson2010erbismuthate)
our_laser: In class: Mary 2013 wrote low-loss symmetric multiscan guides in Yb-bismuthate with an IMRA µJewel D400 at 1047 nm, 350 fs, 1 MHz, ~50 nJ, NA 0.4, 200 µm deep, and Beecher 2010 used 350 fs, 500 kHz, NA 0.4 in Er-bismuthate: cumulative-heating positive-Δn cores that gave Yb lasers above 78 % slope efficiency (Mary 2012) and a 16 dB net-gain Er amplifier (Thomson 2010). Caveat: speed and scan count of the ~50 nJ recipe were not retrieved, and 50 nJ at 1 MHz (~50 mW, our calculation) needs strong attenuation of the CARBIDE.
open_questions:
Commercial availability.
Writing parameters of Thomson 2010 and Mary 2012.
class_note_full: High-index (n = 2.03) heavy-metal-oxide host for Er3+ (1.53-1.56 um) and Yb3+ (~1.04-1.06 um). Laser-inscribed waveguides gave 2.3 dB/cm internal gain and 16 dB net gain (Er), and > 78 % slope-efficiency lasers (Yb).
composition_full: Bi2O3-based oxide glass doped with Er3+ or Yb3+; full composition not retrieved. Yb:BG sample in mary2013graphene: 1.6e26 m^-3 Yb3+.
index_change_full: Positive index change at the focus forms the waveguide (mary2013graphene, arXiv full-text excerpt); multiscan used for symmetric, low-loss guides.
typical_delta_n_full: not reported in the retrieved excerpts
writing_regime_full: MHz, low-energy multiscan: 1047 nm, 350 fs, 1 MHz, ~50 nJ, 0.4 NA, 200 um depth (mary2013graphene). Inside the CARBIDE's range for rep rate (up to 1008 kHz) and wavelength (1025 nm).
best_loss_full: not retrieved as a propagation loss; 4.0 dB total fibre-to-fibre insertion loss for an 87 mm guide at 1618 nm (thomson2010erbismuthate)
dlw_notes_full: In Er-doped bismuthate, ion clustering limited the achievable gain in one substrate composition (Heriot-Watt PhD thesis). fs-written Yb bismuthate guides were also used for a 1.94 GHz CW mode-locked SESAM laser (ASSL 2015 abstract AM5A.22: 30.9 pJ, 1.1 ps).

label: N-SF8
name: SCHOTT N-SF8 dense flint
class_note: Lead-free high-index flint, used as the cladding glass of GLS fibres.
composition: TiO₂–SiO₂-based, lead-free.
index_change: Negative Δn at the focus from network expansion (Type II), so guides need two written lines (Sotillo 2017).
writing_regime: 500 kHz, 50–400 mW, 2–50 mm/s; the glass conducts heat well in 3D (k = 1.03 W/m·K) (Sotillo 2017).
best_loss: 0.7 dB/cm in the near-IR (Sotillo 2017)
dlw_notes: The index decrease was confirmed by micro-Raman and X-ray microanalysis.
our_laser: Sotillo 2017 wrote double-line guides (0.7 dB/cm, near-IR) at 500 kHz, 50–400 mW (100–800 nJ, computed) and 2–50 mm/s, rate and energy inside the CARBIDE's range, but the writing wavelength and pulse duration were not retrieved. Expect negative Δn at the focus from volume expansion, so guide between two closely spaced lines.
open_questions: Writing wavelength and pulse duration.
class_note_full: High-index flint; used as the cladding glass of GLS chalcogenide fibres for nonlinear photonics (Sotillo 2017). n and n2 not retrieved.
composition_full: TiO2–SiO2 based (lead-free dense flint) per Sotillo 2017
index_change_full: Negative Δn near the focal volume (Type II), attributed to volume expansion from glass-network modification → double-line waveguides needed.
writing_regime_full: High rep. rate (500 kHz) writing, 50–400 mW, 2–50 mm/s; authors suggest good 3-D heat flow (k = 1.03 W/m·K).
best_loss_full: 0.7 dB/cm, near-IR (sotillo2017nsf8)
dlw_notes_full: Index decrease confirmed by micro-Raman and X-ray microanalysis.
open_questions_full:
Writing wavelength, pulse duration and objective need the accepted manuscript (eprints.soton.ac.uk/413314, open).
N-SF8 datasheet values (nd, Tg, density, CTE) not retrieved.
No fs-DLW paper on SF57, SF10 or other lead silicates (N-SF) could be identified within the search budget. Leads not included: CSIC record digital.csic.es/handle/10261/21099 (fs-written guides in an alkaline lead-oxide silicate glass; dark non-guiding core above ~14 µJ); SPIE Proc. 5662 (2004), doi 10.1117/12.596350, 'Waveguide structures in heavy metal oxide glasses written with fs…' — authors not retrieved.
ResearchGate 319854557, 'Femtosecond laser processing induced low loss waveguides in multicomponent glasses' (Opt. Mater. Express 2017?) — glasses and authors not confirmed.

label: SF57
name: SCHOTT SF57 (lead silicate)
index_change: In an alkaline lead-oxide silicate glass the index change was linked to network structure and defects; above ~14 µJ the centre stops guiding and guiding zones form at its sides.
our_laser: No recipe in our class with parameters: Fuerbach 2010 wrote fibre-matched Type I guides in SF57 by cumulative heating at >1 MHz with peak power below the self-focusing threshold (source and wavelength not retrieved), and the CSIC Madrid study saw a non-guiding dark central zone above ~14 µJ (an amplified source is implied). The CARBIDE tops out at 1008 kHz, the lower edge of that cumulative regime, so a new low-energy scan at ~1 MHz is needed.
open_questions: No fs-written waveguide paper on SF57, SF10 or SF6 found in a targeted search (October 2026); the one paper found is on a related lead-oxide silicate glass, with incomplete citation.
dlw_notes_full: No fs-written waveguide paper on SCHOTT SF57, SF10 or SF6 found in a targeted search (queries: 'femtosecond laser written waveguides lead silicate glass SF57 OR SF10 OR SF6 heavy flint inscription'; 'ultrafast laser inscription waveguides SF57 glass nonlinear supercontinuum OR loss OR refractive index change'; 'lead silicate glass femtosecond laser direct writing optical waveguides'). One paper on an 'alkaline lead-oxide silicate glass' (DOI 10.1063/1.1994927) was found with incomplete bibliographic data. A UCM record titled 'Raman spectroscopy of femtosecond laser written low propagation loss optical waveguides in Schott N-SF8 glass' also appeared (N-SF8 is a lead-free dense flint, so not entered here; ~0.7 dB/cm NIR per a search summary). Lead-germanate glass results exist but belong to a different family.
open_questions_full: No fs-written waveguide paper collected for this glass.

label: ZBLAN
name: ZBLAN fluorozirconate glass
class_note: Transmits to ~5 µm with low phonon energy (~550–600 cm⁻¹). Weakly nonlinear (n₂ ~10⁻²⁰ m²/W). Its low Tg (~265 °C) makes it melt easily under cumulative heating.
trade_names: ZBLAN (Le Verre Fluoré; University of Adelaide, in-house)
composition: Typically 53 ZrF₄ – 20 BaF₂ – 4 LaF₃ – 3 AlF₃ – 20 NaF (mol%).
index_change: MHz writing melts and quenches the glass and lowers the index, so guides are depressed claddings: rings or arrays of tracks around an unmodified core (Gross 2013). A small positive Type I change (up to ~1.25×10⁻³) is cited from Laval work (Bérubé 2013).
writing_regime: Macquarie/Adelaide use a Ti:sapphire oscillator at 5.1 MHz and assemble the tracks into depressed claddings. Low-rate (5–50 kHz) multiscan gives strong Type I only in modified fluorides (Fernandez 2022). Our 60–1008 kHz range lies between these two regimes.
best_loss: 0.29 ± 0.03 dB/cm at 4 µm, single-mode depressed cladding (Gross 2015)
dlw_notes: Depressed claddings allow very large single-mode cores (up to 45 µm). Bragg gratings (Gross 2012) and 2.5–5 µm beam combiners (Tepper 2017) have been written. Davis 1996 already wrote lines in ZBLAN.
our_laser: No ZBLAN waveguide paper with a laser in our class was found. The closest Yb recipe, PHAROS 1030 nm, ~240 fs, 5–50 kHz multiscan (Fernandez 2022), gives only a very limited positive/negative Δn in standard ZBLAN, while the Macquarie ZBLAN devices (e.g. Gross 2015, 0.29 dB/cm at 4 µm, depressed cladding; its laser not retrieved) rely on negative-Δn tracks, which in Palmer 2013 came from cumulative heating with a 5.1 MHz Ti:sapphire oscillator, above our 1008 kHz maximum. Whether CARBIDE tracks near 1 MHz are negative enough for a depressed cladding needs a new energy/speed scan; the 5–50 kHz window needs the pulse picker.
open_questions: Writing energies and NA of the Macquarie papers.
class_note_full: Low-loss transmission to ~5 µm (bulk) with low phonon energy (~550–600 cm⁻¹). Weakly nonlinear (n2 ~1e-20 m²/W, below fused silica). Very low Tg (~265 °C) makes the glass prone to melting under cumulative heating.
composition_full: Commonly cited 53 ZrF4 – 20 BaF2 – 4 LaF3 – 3 AlF3 – 20 NaF (mol%); varies by maker.
index_change_full: Negative Δn in the focus under MHz (cumulative-heating) writing: local melting and fast quenching open the network and lower the index (gross2013fluorozirconate; palmer2013ybzblan abstract). Waveguides are therefore DEPRESSED-CLADDING structures (rings or hexagonal arrays of modified tracks around an unmodified core). Laval (Bérubé et al. 2013, OME 3, 598) reported a small positive Δn; later papers cite a maximum of ~1.25e-3 (not verified here). Fernandez 2022 says standard ZBLAN gives only very limited positive or negative Δn.
typical_delta_n_full: Negative; magnitude for ZBLAN not retrieved. Positive type I up to ~1.25e-3 reported by Bérubé 2013 (secondary citation).
writing_regime_full: Macquarie/Adelaide devices: Ti:sapphire oscillator at 5.1 MHz (cumulative heating) → negative-Δn tracks assembled into depressed claddings. Low-rep-rate (5–50 kHz, 1030 nm, ~240 fs) multiscan writing gave strong type I only in MODIFIED fluorides, not pure ZBLAN (fernandez2022tailoredfluoride). For a CARBIDE (60–1008 kHz, 1025 nm), expect heat-accumulation behaviour at the high end of its range; the 5–50 kHz window of Fernandez 2022 lies below its stated minimum rep rate.
best_loss_full: 0.29 ± 0.03 dB/cm at 4 µm, single-mode depressed cladding (gross2015zblanmidir)
dlw_notes_full: Depressed-cladding guides allow very large single-mode-like cores (up to 45 µm, M² ≈ 1.1; see rare-earth-doped-zblan). Waveguide Bragg gratings can be written (gross2012zblanbragg). Broadband couplers for 2.5–5 µm astro-interferometry (tepper2017zblancombiner).
open_questions_full:
No DOI here was checked against Crossref: api.crossref.org (and doi.org, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar) were blocked by the session proxy (403), WebFetch had no DNS, and the Consensus quota was used up. Run `curl -s https://api.crossref.org/works/<DOI>` on every paper before publishing.
Laser parameters could not be read from full texts (WebFetch unavailable). Most writing-parameter fields are null and must be filled from the papers.
Bérubé, Bernier, Vallée, Opt. Mater. Express 3(5), 598–611 (2013) (Laval, positive Δn in fluoride glass) is cited by several papers, but its title, abstract and DOI (likely 10.1364/OME.3.000598) were not seen, so it is not in the paper list.
Fluoroindate (IFG-type) glass: no peer-reviewed fs-written planar waveguide paper found. Only a Research Square preprint (rs-8213333, 1 kHz, 500 µm/s channel waveguides, thermal erasure) and a fs-written long-period grating in fluoroindate fibre (Infrared Phys. Technol., ScienceDirect S1350449521001808).
Le Verre Fluoré bulk-ZBLAN datasheet (exact n, Tg, transmission for the supplied glass) not retrieved.
Thermal conductivity / diffusivity and two-photon absorption data for ZBLAN not retrieved.
Whether arriola2017midirmaterials includes ZBLAN in its glass set was not confirmed.

label: Doped ZBLAN
name: Rare-earth-doped ZBLAN (Tm, Ho, Yb, Er)
class_note: Low-phonon host for 1–2.9 µm chip lasers: Yb at 1030 nm (84 % slope), Er at 1.55 µm (25 %), Tm at 1.88–1.89 µm (50–67 % internal slope), Ho at 2.05–2.1 µm (> 1 W) and Ho at 2.9 µm (~20 %).
composition: ZBLAN host doped with Tm³⁺, Ho³⁺, Tm/Ho, Yb³⁺ or Er/Yb/Ce.
index_change: Negative Δn under MHz oscillator writing; all of these lasers use depressed claddings.
writing_regime: Ti:sapphire oscillator at 5.1 MHz, cumulative heating (Palmer 2013). A Macquarie patent gives 800 nm, 5.1 MHz, 550 nJ, 50 fs, NA 1.25.
our_laser: No doped-ZBLAN waveguide written with a Yb laser was found: the retrieved recipe (Palmer 2013: Yb:ZBLAN, 84% slope efficiency, 170 mW) uses depressed claddings of negative-Δn tracks written with a 5.1 MHz Ti:sapphire oscillator (cumulative heating), above our 1008 kHz maximum; the other Tm/Ho/Er chip lasers (Lancaster 2011–2016) use the same geometry with parameters not retrieved. The depressed-cladding layout (cores up to 45 µm, Lancaster 2012) can be copied, but whether 1025 nm pulses at ≤1 MHz give a large enough negative Δn needs a new scan (Fernandez 2022 found standard ZBLAN responds only weakly to PHAROS pulses at 5–50 kHz). Caveat (our inference): in Yb-doped samples the 1025 nm writing beam lies in the Yb band (these lasers emit at 1030 nm per the DFG project report).

Writing parameters of each laser paper.
Dopant concentrations.
class_note_full: Low-phonon-energy host for 1.0–2.9 µm rare-earth lasers. Demonstrated fs-written waveguide lasers: Yb 1030 nm (84% slope), Er 1.55 µm (25%), Tm 1.88–1.89 µm (50–67% internal slope), Ho 2.05–2.1 µm (>1 W), Ho 2.9 µm (~20%).

typical_delta_n_full: Not retrieved; palmer2013ybzblan abstract quotes an index change exceeding 2.3e-2 (glass/sign not resolved in the retrieved text).
writing_regime_full: Ti:sapphire oscillator at 5.1 MHz (palmer2013ybzblan abstract); cumulative heating regime. Other papers' parameters not retrieved.
best_loss_full: Not retrieved for doped guides (undoped ZBLAN: 0.29 dB/cm at 4 µm, gross2015zblanmidir).

label: Tailored fluorides
name: Tailored fluoride glasses (Z/HBLAN, La-free Ba fluoride)
class_note: Fluorides engineered so that writing gives a large positive Δn (10⁻² to > 2×10⁻²), which avoids depressed claddings.
composition: ZBLAN-type glass with HfF₄ as a second former (Z/HBLAN), and a La-free, Ba-containing fluoride.
index_change: Type I positive Δn in the focus.
typical_delta_n: ≈ 10⁻² in Z/HBLAN (Fernandez 2022); > 2×10⁻² in the La-free glass (Fernandez 2024)
writing_regime: PHAROS, 1030 nm, ~240 fs, 5–50 kHz, multiscan (Fernandez 2022).
best_loss: 0.21 dB/cm (Fernandez 2024)
dlw_notes: The mechanism differs: a polarisability change without migration in Z/HBLAN (2022), and Ba-migration densification in the La-free glass (2024).
our_laser: Directly in our class: PHAROS 1030 nm, ~240 fs multiscan type I writing at 5–50 kHz gives Δn ≈ 1e-2 in Z/HBLAN (Fernandez 2022), and at 50 kHz (best of a 1–250 kHz scan), circular polarisation, 0.6 NA 40× with detuned collar, 170 µm deep it gives Δn > 2e-2 and 0.21 dB/cm in a La-free Ba-containing fluoride (Fernandez 2024); the same 1030 nm/240 fs/50 kHz writing made 80:20 couplers for a 2.7 µm Er:ZBLAN fibre ring laser (An 2025). Our 1025 nm and 240 fs match; 50 kHz needs the pulse picker (or a test at our 60 kHz minimum, inside the 1–250 kHz window Fernandez 2024 scanned), and pulse energy and speed were not retrieved, so they need a scan. Caveat: these are research melts (Le Verre Fluoré), and standard ZBLAN does not respond the same way.
open_questions: Pulse energy, NA and speed.
class_note_full: Fluoride glasses whose composition is engineered so that fs writing gives a large POSITIVE Δn (1e-2 to >2e-2), avoiding the depressed claddings needed in standard ZBLAN.
composition_full: ZBLAN-type glasses with HfF4 as a second glass former (Z/HBLAN), and a rare-earth-doped, lanthanum-free fluoride composition; exact mol% not retrieved.
index_change_full: Type I positive Δn in the focus (guiding core).
typical_delta_n_full: ≈1e-2 (Z/HBLAN, fernandez2022tailoredfluoride); >2e-2 in a La-free Ba-containing fluoride (fernandez2024highdnfluoride arXiv abstract; a ResearchGate version quotes 1.3e-2 max)

label: GLS
name: Gallium lanthanum sulphide (GLS)
class_note: Transparent from 0.5 to 10 µm, n ≈ 2.4, χ(3) about 1000× that of fused silica, arsenic-free, Tg ~560 °C. Used for mid-IR beam combiners, supercontinuum and all-optical switching.
trade_names: GLS / GaLaS (University of Southampton ORC; Crystran)
composition: Ga₂S₃–La₂S₃ sulphide glass; GLSSe is the Se-substituted variant.
index_change: A positive Δn core (Type I) from modified Ga–S and La–S bonds (Ramos Vázquez 2019); no depressed cladding needed.
writing_regime: 1030 nm and 500 kHz throughout: BlueCut ~400 fs, NA 0.4, circular polarization, 15–80 nJ (Arriola 2014); PHAROS 230 fs, NA 0.42, multiscan at 70 nJ and 5 mm/s (Ramos Vázquez 2019); multiscan 40–52 nJ at 2–16 mm/s (Mackenzie 2019). All inside our CARBIDE's range.
best_loss: ≈ 0.22 dB/cm at 4 µm, single-mode (Gretzinger 2019)
dlw_notes: Writing conditions tune the waveguide dispersion: zero-dispersion wavelength 3.66–3.71 µm versus 3.61 µm in bulk (Demetriou 2016).

The CARBIDE can copy these directly (1025 nm, 230–400 fs, 500 kHz, tens of nJ). Caveat: these energies are tiny compared with the ~10 µJ available at 500 kHz, so fine, stable attenuation matters; the lowest loss (0.22 dB/cm at 4 µm, Gretzinger 2019) came from a cumulative-heating multiscan process whose laser was not retrieved (a citing paper used a 5.1 MHz Ti:sapphire oscillator).

class_note_full: Transparent 0.5–10 µm, n ≈ 2.4, high χ3 (described as ~1000× fused silica), arsenic-free, high Tg (~560 °C) for a chalcogenide. Used for mid-IR astrophotonic beam combiners, supercontinuum and all-optical switching.
composition_full: Ga2S3–La2S3-based sulphide glass, arsenic-free; the exact ratio varies by maker (not retrieved). GLSSe = Se-substituted variant.
index_change_full: Positive Δn guiding core (type I) reported, from modified Ga–S and La–S bonds (vazquez2019glsnonlinear). Hughes 2009 describes two track types (filamentary, and teardrop type IIA plus heating). Depressed cladding not needed.
typical_delta_n_full: Not retrieved (demetriou2016glsdispersion measured the profiles).
writing_regime_full: In-class recipes, all multiscan at 500 kHz: Menlo BlueCut 1030 nm, ~400 fs, 0.4 NA, circular, ~200 µm deep, 21 scans × 0.3 µm, sweep 15–80 nJ at 2–16 mm/s, optimum 70 nJ at 4 mm/s → 0.8 dB/cm at 3.39 µm (arriola2014glscouplers); PHAROS 1030 nm, 230 fs, 0.42 NA, 18 scans × 0.3 µm, 20–500 nJ at 5–50 mm/s, guide at 70 nJ and 5 mm/s (vazquez2019glsnonlinear); 0.4 NA, circular, 0.33 µm offset, 40–52 nJ, 2–16 mm/s (mackenzie2019glssc). name: Arsenic trisulphide (As₂S₃)
class_note: Strongly nonlinear, mid-IR-transparent chalcogenide; sold as SCHOTT IRG 27.
composition: As₂S₃ (As₄₀S₆₀); As₃₉S₆₁ in Arriola 2017.

label: Ag zinc phosphate
name: Silver-containing zinc phosphate glass (Bordeaux ICMCB / CELIA research glass); related Ag-containing fluorophosphate glass
class_note: Passive photosensitive glass. Type A delta-n ~5e-3, comparable to good Type I glasses.
composition: Research glass melted at ICMCB Bordeaux: silver- and zinc-containing phosphate glass (Ag2O-ZnO-P2O5; Ga2O3 appears in keywords of related ICMCB records). A related silver-nanocluster-doped fluorophosphate glass (UNESP, Brazil) shows the same silver-based writing.
index_change: Type A: positive delta-n from silver clusters around (not in) the focal voxel, so the guiding region is the cluster-rich zone at the voxel periphery; Type I (focus-centre) waveguides can also be written in the same glass at higher pulse energy (SPIE 2018 comparison: Type A similar function to Type I, with advantages incl. thermal stability study). Surface and near-surface Ag waveguides work without extra processing (2019). Amorphous glass: no chi(2), no gain; the silver-cluster fluorescence survives in the guiding region.
writing_regime: Cluster formation is multiphoton (four-photon) driven (bourhis2010silverzincphosphate). A Russian data paper wrote tracks in Ag zinc phosphate at 1030 nm, 180 fs, 1 mm/s while varying rep rate and pulse energy (data2020agzinctracks): close to our CARBIDE 1025 nm.
dlw_notes: Glass is not commercial; samples come from the ICMCB/Bordeaux glass group. Waveguiding was also transposed to ribbon fibres of the same glass (aboukhalil2017typea). Ag fluorophosphate variant can be re-written by overlapping passes (UNESP record).
our_laser: Bordeaux's Type A waveguides (positive Δn up to ~6e-3 from Ag clusters at the voxel periphery; Abou Khalil 2017, Petit 2018) are the target, but their writing parameters were not retrieved here, so their rate regime (MHz vs ≤1 MHz) is unconfirmed. The only in-class data are tracks written at 1030 nm, 180 fs, 1 mm/s at 10, 100 and 500 kHz in Ag zinc phosphate glass (Shakhgildyan 2020), not characterised as waveguides; the CARBIDE covers the 100 and 500 kHz cases at 1025 nm, ≥208 fs (10 kHz needs the pulse picker). Caveat: laser parameters decide whether Type A or Type I forms (Bordeaux comparison, Petit 2018), so energy, speed and rate need a new scan; the glass is a non-commercial ICMCB melt.
open_questions: Exact glass composition (mol%), refractive index, Tg and transmission window of the Bordeaux Ag zinc phosphate glass. Exact title, authors and journal of the SPIE 2018 Type A vs Type I paper and volume/pages of the 2019 near-surface paper. No commercial supplier found; samples would have to come from ICMCB Bordeaux or a collaborating glass lab.

label: Foturan / Foturan II
name: Photostructurable lithium-aluminosilicate glass / glass-ceramic SCHOTT FOTURAN and FOTURAN II (trace Ag, Ce)
class_note: Passive photosensitive glass; its value for DLW is the combination of waveguides with fs-laser-assisted etching of microchannels, mirrors and lenses in one chip (Sugioka/Cheng). No chi(2) or gain.
composition: Photosensitive lithium-aluminosilicate glass containing trace silver (Cheng 2003 abstract; Bhardwaj 2005 calls it a Li-Al-silicate glass).
index_change: Glass state: Type I positive delta-n in the focus works directly (waveguides without thermal crystallization, bhardwaj2005multicomponent; above-breakdown writing gives index increase, li2006foturanwaveguides). Alternative: sub-threshold latent exposure plus anneal at ~500-550 C precipitates Ag nanoparticles in the track and raises the index (cheng2003gratings, li2006foturanwaveguides, optimum particle density for loss). Ceramized state: fs-induced delta-n becomes negative, so a depressed-cladding geometry would be needed. No chi(2)/gain; the Ag-nanoparticle route adds absorption/scattering if over-developed.
writing_regime: Two regimes reported by Li et al. 2006: above optical-breakdown threshold (direct index increase) and well below threshold followed by 500 C anneal. Gratings: tightly focused fs beam below breakdown, then 520 C for 3-18 h (cheng2003gratings).
dlw_notes: Optofluidics: write latent pattern, bake, etch in dilute HF to make buried hollow 3D channels; waveguides, Mach-Zehnder interferometers and attenuators can be added in the same glass (sugioka2012labchipreview). Wang, Sugioka, Hanada, Midorikawa (2007) integrated a waveguide with a micromirror. German lead: DGaO proceedings 'Three dimensional Modification of the Refractive Index in Photosensitive Foturan Glass'. The bake route needs a furnace step (500-550 C) after writing.
our_laser: No Foturan waveguide paper with a Yb laser was found, and the laser parameters of the Foturan waveguide papers were not retrieved (Bhardwaj 2005: positive-Δn guides in the glass state; Li 2006: direct writing above the breakdown threshold, or sub-threshold exposure plus 500 °C anneal precipitating Ag nanoparticles; Cheng 2003: latent gratings baked at 520 °C for 3–18 h). Either route needs a new energy/rate/speed scan at 1025 nm. Keep the material in the glass state, because after ceramization the laser-induced Δn turns negative (Bhardwaj 2005), and an over-developed Ag-nanoparticle route adds absorption/scattering loss (Li 2006).
open_questions: FOTURAN II datasheet values (n at 1 um, Tg, CTE, transmission) - datasheet PDF not readable. Writing parameters, delta-n and loss of fs waveguides in Foturan (Li 2006, Wang 2007/2008, Bhardwaj 2005) - full texts not accessible. Whether as-received FOTURAN II (vs. old FOTURAN) behaves the same under 1025 nm fs writing - no FOTURAN II waveguide paper found. Bibliographic data of Wang, Sugioka, Hanada, Midorikawa 2007 (waveguide + micromirror).

label: Ge:SiO₂ fibre
name: Ge-doped silica: in-fibre writing in standard Ge-doped single-mode fibre (core gratings, cladding waveguides coupled to the core)
class_note: Passive silica; the point is writing gratings, taps and microfluidics directly into an existing fibre so the fibre core is the bus waveguide. No chi(2) or gain (unless a doped fibre is used).
composition: GeO2-doped SiO2 core in a fused-silica cladding (~125 um) of standard, non-photosensitised telecom single-mode fibre; Bulk silica properties: see fused-silica entry.
index_change: Core: Type I positive index modulation (fibre Bragg gratings, point-by-point) in the Ge-doped core without photosensitisation; also through the coating (martinez2006coated). Cladding (pure silica): Type I positive-delta-n waveguides, directional couplers and resonators that couple to the core (herman2013matecfibre). Plus selective etching for buried microchannels (haque2014labinfiber). Amorphous; no chi(2)/gain.
typical_delta_n: bulk Ge-doped silica ~1e-2 after 10 scans (patent US 6977137)
writing_regime: Toronto: frequency-doubled Yb fibre laser at 522 nm, ~200 fs, 500 kHz, 1.25 NA oil immersion focusing through the curved fibre wall. Aston: infrared fs point-by-point, < 60 s per grating. Our 1025 nm CARBIDE would need an oil-immersion objective or index-matching to cancel the cylindrical lensing of the fibre.
dlw_notes: Cylindrical fibre surface acts as a lens; oil-immersion focusing removes it (haque2014labinfiber). Writing through the polymer coating demonstrated for gratings (martinez2006coated). A patent describes a sensitisation route (fs NIR pre-exposure, then UV writing) - not used here.
our_laser: No in-fibre waveguide or grating paper with a 1 µm-fundamental laser in our class was retrieved: Herman 2013 wrote low-loss cladding waveguides and core couplers with a frequency-doubled Yb fibre laser (522 nm, ~200 fs, 500 kHz, 1.25 NA oil immersion), and the Aston point-by-point FBGs (Martinez 2004, 2006) used an IR fs laser whose parameters were not retrieved. Our rate and pulse width match Herman 2013, but without a harmonic module we would write at 1025 nm, so energy and speed need a new scan; an oil-immersion objective is needed to cancel the fibre's cylindrical lensing (Haque 2014).
open_questions: only a patent (US 6977137). Delta-n and loss values of the fibre-cladding waveguides; Ge doping level of the fibres used. Full author lists and DOIs of the Aston Electron. Lett. 2004 and Opt. Lett. 2006 papers. Fibre suppliers not searched.
