label: Bi-doped silicate
name: Bismuth-doped silicate glass (broadband NIR-emitting Bi centres)
composition: Bi-doped silicate glass.
index_change: Type I positive delta-n in the focus, up to 4.3e-3, single-scan and multiscan cores nearly mode-matched to telecom fibre. Bi NIR fluorescence is still detected from the waveguides, so the active centres survive in the guiding region. Amorphous; no chi(2).
dlw_notes: Leads not added as papers (bibliographic data incomplete): fs-laser-induced Bi NIR emission in borosilicate glass (Photonics Research 7(3), 300 (2019)); fs-written active waveguides in porous glass impregnated with Bi (ITMO). Bi-doped commercial bulk glass not found.
our_laser: The only Bi-doped-glass waveguide paper (Psaila 2006: single- and multiscan type I guides, Δn up to 4.3e-3, nearly mode-matched to telecom fibre, Bi fluorescence at 1.3 µm preserved) did not yield its laser parameters, so it is not confirmed to be in our class. The same Heriot-Watt group wrote Er:Yb oxyfluoride guides with a diode-pumped Yb:glass oscillator at 600 kHz (Psaila 2008), inside our rate range; our inference is that a multiscan start near 500 kHz–1 MHz is reasonable, but energy and speed need a new scan.
open_questions: Host composition, Bi content, n and Tg of the Heriot-Watt glass; writing laser parameters and loss. No fs-written waveguide in Bi-doped germanate glass was found; only one Bi-silicate waveguide paper verified. No commercial source of Bi-doped bulk glass found.

label: Oxyfluoride / borate
name: Er(/Yb)-doped oxyfluoride silicate glasses and transparent nano-glass-ceramics; Er-doped Li-Zn fluoroborate glass
class_note: Er3+ (and Er/Yb) in low-phonon fluoride environments for C-band gain; fs-written Er:Yb oxyfluoride silicate waveguide gave 0.72 dB net gain at 1537 nm over 10 mm (psaila2007amplifier).
composition: Research glasses: Er3+/Yb3+-doped oxyfluoride silicate glass (Heriot-Watt); Er- and Er/Yb-doped oxyfluoride glasses and nano-glass-ceramics (fluoride nanocrystals in a silicate glass; Aston 2008, Salamanca/CFM 2020); Er-doped Li-Zn fluoroborate glass (Thomas et al. 2015).
index_change: Type I positive delta-n core in the focus in all three hosts: ~0.006 at 800 nm in Er/Yb oxyfluoride nano-glass-ceramic (single-mode, near-Gaussian modes, Y-splitters and MZIs in 2D/3D), 3-6e-3 in Li-Zn fluoroborate glass. Gain survives in the guiding region (net gain in oxyfluoride silicate glass; Er emission guided in the nano-glass-ceramic).
writing_regime: Both work: low rep rate 1 kHz, 0.34 uJ, 20 um/s for the nano-glass-ceramic (no annealing); high rep rate 500 kHz, 1 MHz and 2 MHz in fluoroborate; 11 MHz, 54 fs, 795 nm oscillator at 13-26 nJ for Er oxyfluoride glass/NGC (wong2008oxyfluoride). Multiscan used to lower loss in oxyfluoride silicate glass (psaila2007amplifier).
best_loss: 1.6 dB/cm
dlw_notes: Glasses are research melts; no commercial supplier found. Our CARBIDE at 60-1000 kHz could cover both the kHz and the 500 kHz-1 MHz windows reported.
our_laser: In class: Er:Yb oxyfluoride silicate waveguide lasers were written with a diode-pumped Yb:glass oscillator at 600 kHz using multiscan (Psaila 2008; wavelength, energy and speed not retrieved), and the related multiscan amplifier gave 1.2 dB background insertion loss and 0.72 dB net gain at 1537 nm (Psaila 2007); Er Li-Zn fluoroborate guides with Δn 3–6e-3 were written at 500 kHz, 1 MHz and 2 MHz with 200–1000 nJ (Thomas 2015; wavelength not confirmed). The CARBIDE covers 500 kHz–1 MHz and these energies (type I, cumulative-heating regime) but not 2 MHz; the nano-glass-ceramic recipe (Vázquez de Aldana 2020: 1 kHz, 0.34 µJ, 20 µm/s, Δn ~6e-3, 1.6 dB/cm) needs the pulse picker. Caveat: at high rate ions migrate (B and Zn enrich the core, F moves to the heat-affected zone; Thomas 2015).
open_questions: Compositions, n, Tg and phonon energy of the hosts; whether fluoride nanocrystals survive in the written core of the nano-glass-ceramic. Laser wavelength/duration of the 2020 Salamanca work; loss value of the fluoroborate waveguides. Full bibliographic data (volume/pages, DOIs) of the Heriot-Watt APL 2005/2007 and Aston 2008 papers. No commercial supplier of Er oxyfluoride glass-ceramic or fluoroborate glass found.

label: ZERODUR / ULE
name: Ultra-low-expansion materials: SCHOTT ZERODUR (Li-Al-silicate glass-ceramic) and Corning ULE 7972 (TiO2-SiO2 glass)
class_note: Passive; chosen for thermal stability of the circuit (ULE CTE 0 +/- 30 ppb/C; ZERODUR near-zero CTE) for space-borne astronomy, interferometry and quantum optics (guan2020zerodur).
composition: ZERODUR: lithium-aluminosilicate glass-ceramic (crystalline phase in a residual glass; Bhardwaj 2005 groups it with Foturan and Robax as LAS). ULE 7972: titania-silicate glass.
index_change: ZERODUR / LAS glass-ceramic: in ceramized LAS the fs-induced delta-n is negative (bhardwaj2005multicomponent); 10 kHz pulses amorphize the crystals with delta-n ~ -0.0035, so depressed-cladding waveguides (lipatiev2021depressedlas) or channel guides bounded by amorphized tracks are used; Type II waveguides and mode control reported (photonics2025las). Guan (2020) wrote single-mode waveguides and a directional coupler in bulk ZERODUR at 1 MHz. Crystallinity is destroyed in the written tracks; in depressed-cladding geometry the guiding core stays crystalline (unmodified). ULE: no fs-written waveguide paper found.
writing_regime: Both reported: 1 MHz cumulative regime (514 nm, 170 fs, NA 0.5, circular polarization) in ZERODUR (guan2020zerodur); 10 kHz amorphization regime in near-zero-expansion LAS glass-ceramic (naumov2023lasamorphization).
best_loss: <= 1.5 dB/cm at 777 nm, single-mode (guan2020zerodur)
dlw_notes: Our 1025 nm CARBIDE at 1 MHz is close to the Guan rep-rate regime (he used 514 nm, so pulse energies do not transfer directly).
our_laser: No ZERODUR/ULE waveguide paper at a 1 µm fundamental was retrieved: Guan 2020 wrote single-mode guides (≤1.5 dB/cm at 777 nm) and a coupler in bulk ZERODUR at 514 nm, 170 fs, 1 MHz, 0.5 NA, circular, i.e. our rate and pulse class but frequency-doubled, so without a harmonic module the energy at 1025 nm needs a new scan. In LAS glass-ceramics the fs-induced Δn is negative (amorphization: −0.0035 at 10 kHz, Naumov 2023; up to −0.005, Lipatiev 2021), so depressed-cladding, double-line (optimum 30 µm spacing at 120 mW writing power, Photonics 2025 12, 797) or tubular guides are the geometry; 10 kHz needs the pulse picker and the lasers of these papers were not retrieved; for ULE no fs-written waveguide paper was found.

label: LiNbO₃-in-LNS glass
name: LiNbO₃ crystals laser-grown inside lithium niobium silicate (LNS) and lithium niobium borosilicate (LNSB) glass
class_note: The glass is isotropic (no χ(2)); χ(2) exists only in the laser-grown LiNbO₃ crystal or oriented nanocrystals, shown by SHG at 515 nm. A 3D-written crystal line could act as a χ(2) waveguide inside glass.
composition: Research melts, mol%: 35Li₂O-35Nb₂O₅-30SiO₂ (veenhuizen2017grisc); 37Li₂O-37Nb₂O₅-26SiO₂ (Lehigh, Er-doped variant studied); 33Li₂O-33Nb₂O₅-13SiO₂-21B₂O₃ (LNSB, ari2023lnsb); SiO₂ partly replaced by up to 21 mol% B₂O₃ (muzi2021oriented). No commercial source found.
index_change: Other: cumulative heating grows a LiNbO₃ crystal line in the focus; the crystallised region is the χ(2) element and the intended guide. Veenhuizen 2017 found speed/power-density windows for single-crystal lines with nucleation ahead of the moving focus (avoids polycrystallinity from growth behind it) and predicted a graded index. Lehigh reports guides 'long enough for practical applications' in 37Li₂O-37Nb₂O₅-26SiO₂ glass. Paris-Saclay grows oriented nanocrystals whose polar axis follows the writing polarisation (muzi2021oriented). Crystallinity and χ(2) exist only in the laser-grown region.
writing_regime: Cumulative heating needed: high repetition rates heat the focal volume to hundreds-thousands of K (veenhuizen2017grisc); 200 kHz worked, 1 kHz gave only cracks (KAKENHI). A review figure lists 1030 nm, 300 fs, NA 0.6 for Li₂O-Nb₂O₅-SiO₂ crystallisation (secondary). Bulk sample temperature also controls growth (Lehigh Er-doped study). Writing is slow (≤ 20 µm/s for precipitation in one report). Our CARBIDE (1025 nm, 60-1008 kHz) covers this regime.
dlw_notes: Material must be melted in-house or obtained from the research groups. Glass composition changes laser crystallisation.
our_laser: Inside our range: Paris-Saclay grows LiNbO₃ nanocrystals in LNS/LNSB glass with 1030 nm fs pulses (He 2020: 1030 nm, 300 fs; Muzi 2021, Ari 2023: 1030 nm with energy, rate and polarisation varied), and the Lehigh patent on graded-index single-crystal waveguides (US 10345626, Jain/Dierolf/Veenhuizen; secondary source) lists a PHAROS at 1026 nm, 200 kHz, 175 fs with a 50×/NA 0.6 objective — all within CARBIDE (≤25.5 µJ at 200 kHz). This is the cumulative-heating regime (200 kHz worked, 1 kHz gave cracks; Veenhuizen 2017 found speed/power windows for single-crystal lines with a graded index), and the expected result is a χ(2)-active crystal line whose polar axis can follow the writing polarisation in LNSB (Muzi 2021). Caveat: growth is slow (µm/s scale) and the glass is not commercial; LNSB tolerated ~5× faster scanning than LNS.
open_questions: No commercial LNS/LNSB glass found; vendor rows left empty. Titles of he2020crystals and ari2023lnsb not shown in results; Veenhuizen et al. 2022 (Opt. Mater., glass-composition effect) and the Barker/Jain/Dierolf Er-doped study seen only as summaries, not included.

label: LaBGeO₅
name: LaBGeO₅ (stillwellite) ferroelectric single-crystal lines laser-grown in lanthanum borogermanate glass
class_note: Ferroelectric crystal with small d coefficients (about 1-1.4 pm/V, roughly 20x below LiNbO₃) grown as a single-crystal line inside its parent glass; frequency conversion demonstrated in the written guide (lipatiev2017cgd).
composition: Lanthanum borogermanate glass of (or near) LaBGeO₅ stoichiometry; research melts (Lehigh; Mendeleev University).
index_change: Other: a high-repetition-rate fs laser grows an oriented LaBGeO₅ single-crystal line in the glass by cumulative heating; the crystal line itself guides and keeps χ(2). Single-crystal-in-glass waveguides with 2.64 dB/cm at 1530 nm and uniform cross-section (stone2015waveguide); SHG in the waveguiding mode with an elliptical beam waist (lipatiev2017cgd). Partial remelting (vitrification) of the track along a sinusoidal path at 200 kHz trims the crystalline core to about 1:1 aspect ratio (lipatiev2023remelt).
writing_regime: Cumulative heating at high repetition rate: 'high-repetition-rate femtosecond laser' (stone2009directional); 200 kHz (lipatiev2023remelt). Our CARBIDE repetition-rate range covers this.
best_loss: 2.64 dB/cm at 1530 nm (stone2015waveguide)
dlw_notes: An elliptical beam waist (instead of circular) made continuous crystalline tracks more homogeneous (lipatiev2017cgd). Lines can bend in 3D while keeping c-axis along the line (stone2009directional).
our_laser: Inside our range: the Mendeleev group writes and remelts LaBGeO₅ crystal-in-glass tracks with a PHAROS-SP at 1030 nm and 200 kHz (Lipatiev 2023), and found that quasi-single-crystalline lines grow at ≥25 kHz with 18 µJ (1030 nm, 300 fs; Lipateva 2014); CARBIDE gives 18 µJ up to ~280 kHz. This cumulative-heating regime yields χ(2)-active single-crystal waveguides (2.64 dB/cm at 1530 nm, Stone 2015; SHG in the guided mode with an elliptical waist, Lipatiev 2017). Caveat: nucleation was reported at ≥9 kHz with 110 µJ, above our 85 µJ maximum, so seeding at ≤85 µJ and ≥60 kHz must be tested; the glass is not commercial.
open_questions: No commercial LaBGeO₅ glass found; vendor rows left empty.

label: LiNbO₃ / PPLN
name: Lithium niobate LiNbO₃ (congruent and MgO-doped MgO:LN; z-cut / x-cut; periodically poled PPLN)
class_note: Non-centrosymmetric ferroelectric: d33 about 25-27 pm/V and r33 about 31-32 pm/V (vendor/paper values above), periodically poled for QPM (PPLN). Transparent to about 5 µm, so mid-IR guides are possible (nguyen2016midir).
trade_names: LiNbO₃ crystals, substrates, wafers (SurfaceNet GmbH), Lithium niobate wafers (congruent, optical grade) (Coherent (formerly II-VI)), PPLN / MgO:PPLN (Raicol Crystals)
composition: Single-crystal LiNbO₃, trigonal, space group R3c (SurfaceNet data sheet). Commercial grades: congruent LN and MgO-doped LN; MgO doping up to 4.5-5.0 mol% is quoted for photorefractive-damage suppression.
index_change: Several geometries work, and the choice decides whether χ(2)/r33 survive. (1) Modification in the focus: Thomson et al. 2006 (z-cut, low-repetition-rate regime) got two structure types depending on pulse energy, one guiding in a modified region at the focus and one guiding around a visible damage zone; the latter confined strongly at 1550 nm but the guiding was temporary (stress relaxation). Osellame et al. 2007 wrote multiscan guides in PPLN that kept the nonlinear coefficient (SHG at 1567 nm, 18 %/W). A Fraunhofer record of a 2007 Burghoff/Nolte conference paper reports frequency doubling of 1064 nm in one of the two waveguide types only. (2) Double-line (stress-guided): dual-line guides in z-cut MgO:LN had an optical-damage threshold at 532 nm about 10x higher than cladding guides (lv2016mgoln). (3) Depressed cladding (damage tracks around an unmodified crystalline core): guides both polarisations (lv2016mgoln; qi2016pi with slit shaping, single-mode; wang2017deep down to 1400 µm depth with aberration correction) and keeps the electro-optic effect (r33 = 23.21 pm/V, kroesen2014bragg).
writing_regime: Thomson 2006 worked in the 'low repetition rate regime'; the related Salamanca/Shandong cladding work in LiTaO₃ (wang2019ppmglt) is also described as low-repetition-rate writing. A Heriot-Watt record mentions a separate high-repetition-rate study of devices in z-cut LN.
best_loss: 0.51 (TM) / 0.56 (TE) dB/cm at 1550 nm, circular-packing depressed cladding in x-cut LN (Bhardwaj et al., cited in the arXiv version of qi2016pi; secondary). 0.6 dB/cm with 1.1 dB/facet coupling in z-cut LN (Osellame group, SPIE 2008 abstract; secondary). 0.94 dB/cm at 632.8 nm (lv2016mgoln, depressed cladding).
dlw_notes: Use MgO:LN or keep visible light low: undoped LN suffers photorefractive damage; written guides were tested for 532 nm optical damage (lv2016mgoln). Stress-guided structures can relax over time (thomson2006zcut). Type I/stress guides are often polarisation dependent, depressed claddings guide both polarisations. Aberration correction allowed writing to 1400 µm depth (wang2017deep). Mid-IR stressed-cladding guides were modelled from mode sizes and losses (nguyen2016midir); a thesis of that group says earlier LN cladding guides beyond 3 µm mostly guided one polarisation with about 3 dB/cm (secondary).

label: LiTaO₃ / PPSLT
name: Lithium tantalate LiTaO₃ (congruent CLT, stoichiometric SLT, MgO:SLT; periodically poled PPSLT / PP MgO:LT)
class_note: Ferroelectric like LiNbO₃ but with lower d33, similar r33 (30-34 pm/V), a UV edge near 0.27-0.28 µm and better photorefractive resistance (SLT, MgO:SLT); SLT has a low coercive field (< 1.0 kV/mm).

composition: Single-crystal LiTaO₃; congruent and stoichiometric (SLT, MgO:SLT) grades sold.
index_change: Depressed cladding (circular, written with low-repetition-rate fs pulses) in PP MgO:LT and in fan-out PP MgO:SLT guides both e and o polarisations (with different performance) and keeps χ(2): QPM SHG 0.74 %/(W·cm²) (wang2019ppmglt) and 3.55 %/(W·cm²), 54.3 % peak (li2019fanout). Dual-line stress guides (TE guidance) formed in one step by self-induced multiple refocusing (li2019refocus).
writing_regime: Low-repetition-rate fs writing.
best_loss: minimum insertion loss about 0.54 dB at 1064 nm for fan-out PPSLT cladding guides (li2019fanout)
dlw_notes: QPM temperature depends on poling period and cladding geometry (wang2019ppmglt). Nonlinear propagation creates several foci a few µm apart along the beam; their number, spacing and track length depend on the laser parameters (li2019refocus).
our_laser: No LiTaO₃ paper in our class was found: the PP MgO:LT / fan-out PPSLT depressed claddings were written in a 'low-repetition-rate' regime with 0.75 mm/s for the best guide (Wang 2019), other values not retrieved. Caveat: nonlinear propagation splits the focus into several foci along the beam, whose number depends on the laser parameters (Li 2019 refocus), so track shape must be checked.

label: KTP / PPKTP
name: Potassium titanyl phosphate KTiOPO₄ (KTP), periodically poled PPKTP (isomorph RTP: no fs-writing paper found)
class_note: Biaxial ferroelectric with d33 = 16.9 pm/V and r33 = 35-36 pm/V; periodically poled (PPKTP) for QPM; type-II birefringent SHG of 1064 nm was used in the written guides (nie2016splitter).
trade_names: KTP crystals (LASER COMPONENTS), KTP (KTiOPO₄) (MolTech GmbH), KTP / HGTR KTP (gray-track resistant) (4Lasers)
composition: KTiOPO₄ single crystal (flux-grown or hydrothermal). Flux-grown KTP always contains many potassium vacancies (study cited below).
index_change: Depressed cladding (ring of fs tracks around a track-free core) keeps χ(2): type-II SHG 1064 -> 532 nm in straight guides and 1x4 splitters (nie2016splitter), near-single-mode hybrid cores (nie2018ktp), straight guides and Y-branches (li2024ktp). Heriot-Watt wrote single-mode guides in PPKTP with first- and third-order QPM SHG. In a Nd:YVO₄ + KTP hybrid, micro-photoluminescence and SH confocal images indicated that nonlinear and laser properties survived (hybrid2011ktp).
writing_regime: Heriot-Watt group page: pulse energy 1.4 µJ and writing speed 50 µm/s for one PPKTP guide (rep rate and wavelength not shown).
best_loss: minimum insertion loss about 2.0 dB at 1064 nm (li2024ktp)
dlw_notes: Mind gray tracking for visible SHG at high repetition rate (bulk property). RTP: no fs-written waveguide paper found.

label: Nd:YAG
name: Nd:YAG (Nd3+:Y3Al5O12) single crystal
class_note: Four-level Nd3+ gain at 1064 nm under 808 nm diode pumping. fs-written waveguide lasers reach 384 mW and 46.1% slope efficiency (liu2013doublecladding) and 181 mW / 44% in ceramic (liu2012ceramic).
trade_names: Nd:YAG laser rods / crystals (FEE GmbH (now part of Coherent))
composition: Y3Al5O12 garnet doped with Nd3+ on Y sites; 0.3 at.% Nd in okhrimchuk2012lowloss, Nd(1%):YAG in the Hamburg thesis; FEE stock 0.1-1.8 at.%.
index_change: Two geometries work: (1) double-line, stress-guided (siebenmorgen2009stress: guiding in stress-induced regions around pairs of tracks, with stress-induced birefringence); (2) depressed cladding, a ring of parallel low-index tracks around an unmodified core (okhrimchuk2005depressed, okhrimchuk2012lowloss), also nested double cladding (liu2013doublecladding). The core stays crystalline and the Nd3+ emission is preserved (liu2012ceramic, fluorescence imaging); lasing proves gain survives.
typical_delta_n: ~1e-3 maximum in the centre of double-track waveguides (siebenmorgen2010thesis)
writing_regime: elliptical beam waist for the 0.12 dB/cm cladding (okhrimchuk2012lowloss).
best_loss: 0.12 dB/cm, depressed cladding, 0.3 at.% Nd:YAG (okhrimchuk2012lowloss; wavelength not stated in abstract). Double-line: ~0.6 dB/cm (siebenmorgen2010thesis).
dlw_notes: Depressed claddings give large, near-circular, polarisation-tolerant multimode cores well matched to diode pumping; double-line guides are smaller and polarisation dependent. Croitoru/Pavel (croitoru2018qswitch, listed under nd-vanadate and sesquioxide-ceramic) used 100 µm claddings for Q-switching. Hamburg thesis (Calmano) also reports Q-switched Nd:YAG/Cr4+:YAG waveguides with 1 µJ, 1 ns pulses.
our_laser: Closest in-class recipe: Gebremichael (SPIE PC11988) wrote double-track Nd:YAG waveguides with fs pulses at 1030 nm (and 515 nm) and got efficient single-mode CW lasing at 1064 nm for 15 and 30 µm track separation (rate, energy, speed not retrieved). With CARBIDE the targets are double-track stress guides (Δn ≈ 1e-3, ~0.6 dB/cm, Siebenmorgen 2010) or depressed claddings (0.12 dB/cm, Okhrimchuk 2012); there is no positive-Δn core in the focus and the Nd³⁺ gain survives in the unmodified crystal (Liu 2012). Caveat: none of the listed Nd:YAG papers gives a full rate/energy/speed recipe, so a new scan is needed; double tracks are polarisation dependent.

The core stays crystalline and the Nd3+ emission is preserved (liu2012ceramic, fluorescence imaging); lasing proves gain survives.

Repetition rate, energy and speed were not retrieved for any Nd:YAG paper, so kHz vs MHz suitability cannot be stated from these sources.

class_note: Quasi-three-level Yb3+ gain at 1030 nm with small quantum defect. fs-written Yb:YAG waveguide lasers reached 2.35 W with M² < 1.3 under diode pumping (calmano2011diode).
composition: Y3Al5O12 garnet doped with Yb3+; 7 at.% Yb in the Hamburg waveguide lasers (calmano2011diode); datasheet range 0.5-25 at.%.
index_change: Same as Nd:YAG: no Type I core. Double-track (stress-guided) waveguides from Hamburg (siebenmorgen2010thesis, calmano2011diode) and tubular depressed cladding (tang2015tubular). Gain survives in the unmodified crystalline core (watt-level lasing).

writing_regime: Note: Yb:YAG emits at 1030 nm, close to our 1025 nm writing wavelength, and as a quasi-three-level medium it has some ground-state absorption there; measure sample transmission at 1025 nm before writing, especially at high Yb doping.

dlw_notes: Search summaries of the Hamburg theses mention a Ti:sapphire-pumped 1030 nm waveguide laser with 79% slope efficiency, 1055 mW, and semiconductor-pumped 2.4 W / 51%; the summary did not make clear which thesis (Siebenmorgen or Calmano) it was quoting, so these values are not attached to a paper.

Sin. 2014), whose τ and rate (by pulse picking) CARBIDE matches, and a Hamburg dissertation (K. Expected result is a double-line stress guide or depressed cladding with the Yb gain kept (Calmano 2011, Tang 2015); in Yb:YAG ceramic, laser annealing in the thermal regime halved the loss (Benayas 2011). Caveat: Yb:YAG absorbs near our 1025 nm writing wavelength (quasi-three-level, no number retrieved), so measure transmission at 1025 nm before writing, especially at 7 % Yb.

label: Ti:sapphire
name: Ti:sapphire (Ti3+:Al2O3) single crystal
class_note: Broadband vibronic Ti3+ gain (650-1100 nm), pumped in the green. fs-written double-line waveguides lase CW at 798 nm with 23.5% slope and 170 nm tuning, and give 41 fs pulses at 21 GHz when graphene mode-locked.
composition: α-Al2O3 (sapphire) doped with Ti3+; 0.12 wt.% Ti2O3 in grivas2012tisapphire; Crytur range 0.05-0.3 wt.% Ti2O3.
index_change: Double-line (stress-guided) waveguides between pairs of tracks, 15-24 µm apart (grivas2012tisapphire); no Type I core reported. Ti3+ gain survives in the guiding region (CW lasing, 23.5% slope). fs-written guides worked much better than ps-written ones (23.5% vs 7.1% slope).
writing_regime: Yb-based 1030 nm sources at 1 kHz (180 fs, regen) and 200 kHz (320 fs) were used, plus 8 ps at 200 kHz (grivas2012tisapphire, conference/preprint version). This is the closest match to our CARBIDE (1025 nm, 60-1008 kHz, ≥208 fs) of all crystals in this family. NA 0.65, ~150 µm depth, polarisation parallel to scan.
dlw_notes: Sapphire is very hard with high thermal conductivity (33 W/m·K); stress fields from the tracks give the guiding. Mode-locked waveguide lasers at 21 GHz (grivas2018gigahertz).
our_laser: Inside our range: Grivas 2012 wrote double-line Ti:sapphire waveguide lasers with 1030 nm Yb:KGW pulses at either 320 fs / 200 kHz (65 nJ, 2 mm/s) or 180 fs / 1 kHz (1.5 µJ), NA 0.65, ~150 µm depth, track pairs 15–24 µm apart; both fit CARBIDE (1 kHz by pulse picking). Expected result is a stress-guided double-line waveguide with Ti³⁺ gain kept; the best laser (143 mW, 23.5 % slope at ~798 nm) came from the 180 fs / 1 kHz structures, ps-written ones were worse (7.1 %). Caveat: the slope of the 200 kHz structures was not retrieved, and no Δn or loss value is given.

class_note: Strong π-polarised Nd3+ absorption at 808 nm and emission at 1064 nm. fs-written Nd:GdVO4 channel waveguides reached 70% slope efficiency, near the quantum-defect limit (tan2010gdvo4).
trade_names: YVO4 / Nd:YVO4 crystals (Molecular Technology GmbH (MolTech, Berlin)), Nd:GdVO4 crystals (LASER COMPONENTS GmbH)

label: Pr:LiLuF₄ / Pr:YLF
name: Pr3+-doped fluoride crystals for visible lasers (Pr:LiLuF4, Pr:LiYF4)
class_note: Pr3+ gives direct visible laser lines (green 523, orange 604, red 640, deep red 698/721 nm) under blue InGaN diode pumping. fs-written Pr:LiLuF4 waveguides reach 310 mW at 721 nm (50% slope).

index_change: Depressed-index cladding in Pr:LiLuF4 (baiocco2023prllf); double-line (paired tracks) guiding in Pr:LiYF4 with emission properties preserved (Appl. Phys. B record https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00340-011-4406-6, title not seen). Visible gain survives in the core (lasing, M² = 1.1 single-mode at 721 nm).
best_loss: 0.12 dB/cm in fs-written Pr:LiLuF4 waveguides (Photonics 2023 paper, title not seen; https://gredos.usal.es/handle/10366/156206)

Caveat: fluorides are soft with low thermal conductivity (≈6 W/m·K for YLF) and no high-rate writing data were retrieved for Pr hosts.

label: Sapphire (Al₂O₃)
name: Sapphire (undoped α-Al₂O₃ single crystal)
class_note: Wide-gap (9.9 eV, Alkor) passive crystal transparent from 0.17 to 5.5 µm (Crystran), so it covers visible to mid-IR (2.85 µm single-mode guides shown by Laval). High index (≈1.75 at 1.06 µm) and birefringent. Passive (no gain) unless doped; Ti:sapphire is a separate laser crystal.
composition: Undoped single-crystal α-Al₂O₃, uniaxial (birefringent: no and ne given separately by Crystran).
index_change: Negative Δn: a review quoted by web search states that fs damage lowers the refractive index of sapphire, so a guiding core in the focus does not work. All waveguides found are depressed cladding (single- or multi-layer rings of tracks); the core is unirradiated crystal, so it stays crystalline. No Type I core or double-line stress guide in undoped sapphire was found.
writing_regime: Graz/Infineon optimised energy, pulse duration and repetition rate (values not seen); Oxford used adaptive-optics aberration correction to write multi-layer claddings down to 400–800 µm depth.
best_loss: ≈0.6 dB/cm at 780 nm and ≈0.7 dB/cm at 1550 nm, single-mode (wang2024sapphireplatform)
dlw_notes: Excess loss attributed to sub-wavelength nano-scatterers in the cladding (Oxford). Bend loss rises sharply below 15 mm radius (Winkler 2024). Bragg gratings >90 % reflectivity written with modulated bursts (Oxford).
our_laser: No undoped-sapphire paper with a retrieved in-class recipe: Winkler 2024 (1.9 dB/cm at 728 nm, core 200 µm deep) and Wang 2024 (0.6 dB/cm at 780 nm, adaptive optics, down to 400–800 µm) optimised energy, duration and rate but those values were not retrieved. The closest documented in-class recipe is in Ti:sapphire (Grivas 2012: 1030 nm, 320 fs, 200 kHz, 65 nJ, 2 mm/s, NA 0.65; double lines); for undoped sapphire the working geometry is a depressed cladding of negative-Δn tracks, so energy and track spacing need a new scan. Caveat: deep writing needs aberration correction (Wang 2024) and bend loss rises sharply below 15 mm radius (Winkler 2024).

label: Diamond (SC-CVD)
name: Diamond (single-crystal CVD, optical / electronic / quantum grade)
class_note: Very high index (≈2.42 at 589 nm, Crystran) and extreme thermal conductivity (>2000 W/m/K, Element Six). Transparent from the UV to the far-IR (Element Six: 0.22 to >50 µm; Crystran shows a gap at 2.5–7 µm). Mid-IR waveguides demonstrated (Bharadwaj 2018). Main interest: NV colour centres for quantum photonics.
trade_names: DNV-B1, DNV-B14 (quantum grades with controlled NV density) (Element Six (De Beers Group)), Single crystal diamond, optical grade (Coherent (formerly II-VI))
composition: Carbon, cubic. Quantum work uses single-crystal CVD plates; one Element Six specification quoted in a paper: electronic-grade substrate with <5 ppb N and NV, plus a 40 µm (001) CVD overgrowth layer. Element Six DNV-B14 has >10× the NV density of DNV-B1.
index_change: No positive Type I core. The focus breaks diamond down to a graphitic phase, and the stress-induced index change around it guides light (Courvoisier 2016). Waveguides are type II double lines (stress-guided, e.g. 13 µm or 30 µm separation); multi-line 'Type III' guides support both polarizations. The guiding region between the lines is unmodified crystal: NV properties inside the guides stay high quality (Sotillo 2016), and the waveguides survive the high-temperature anneal used to form NV⁻ (Hadden 2018).
writing_regime: Milan (Eaton): frequency-doubled Yb:KGW at 515 nm, 230 fs, 500 kHz, 1.25-NA oil objective; high NA chosen to avoid self-focusing (critical power ≈2 MW at 515 nm). Oxford (Salter/Booth): 790 nm, 100 fs, 1 kHz Ti:sapphire with SLM aberration correction, which lowered the needed energy from a 110 nJ threshold (uncorrected, 50 µm depth) to below 30 nJ. No diamond waveguide written at ≈1030 nm was found.
best_loss: 4.2 dB/cm at 635 nm (type II, 13 µm separation; hadden2018diamond)
dlw_notes: Oxford corrects the spherical aberration of focusing into diamond with an SLM, which lowers the energy needed and enables 3D structures. Same fs setup writes NV centres and waveguides, so the two can be aligned within micrometres. Bragg-grating waveguides also shown (Bharadwaj 2017).

https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5066270
https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.00170
https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.05885

https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5066270 ; https://arxiv.org/pdf/1701.05885 ; https://arxiv.org/pdf/1806.05412 ; https://doi.org/10.1063/1.4959267
our_laser: No diamond waveguide written at ≈1030 nm was found: Milan (Sotillo 2016, Hadden 2018, Bharadwaj 2018) uses a frequency-doubled PHAROS at 515 nm, 230 fs, 500 kHz with a 1.25-NA oil objective, and Oxford (Courvoisier 2016) uses 790 nm, 100 fs, 1 kHz with SLM aberration correction (<30 nJ). CARBIDE matches Milan's rate and pulse duration but has no 515 nm harmonic, so writing at 1025 nm is an untested recipe; if it works the expected result is type II double-line stress guides around graphitic tracks (4.2 dB/cm at 635 nm, Hadden 2018; 6 dB/cm at 2.4 µm, Bharadwaj 2018). Caveat: Milan chose 500 kHz to reduce absorbing graphite and the high NA to avoid self-focusing at 515 nm, and neither choice has been tested at 1025 nm.

label: ZnSe / ZnS
name: Zinc selenide / zinc sulfide (CVD polycrystalline or single crystal; undoped and Cr²⁺/Fe²⁺-doped)
class_note: ZnSe transmits 0.6–21 µm with n ≈ 2.49 at 1 µm and 2.40 at 10.6 µm (Crystran). Undoped material is passive; Cr²⁺- or Fe²⁺-doped ZnSe/ZnS gives mid-IR gain (Cr:ZnSe waveguide lasers at 2.49–2.57 µm, up to 45 % slope; Cr:ZnS at 2.24 µm).
composition: ZnSe: CVD polycrystalline, zinc-blende (FCC) structure, density 5.27 g/cm³ (Crystran). Laser papers use Cr²⁺- (and Fe²⁺-) doped polycrystalline material.
index_change: Depressed cladding is the working geometry for the mid-IR lasers (Cr:ZnSe, Heriot-Watt) and for ZnS mid-IR guides (Chen/Vázquez de Aldana; NTNU). A helical (tubular) cladding trajectory was used in Cr:ZnS (SIOM). The first near-IR ZnSe guide was multiscan-written; Gain survives in the core: lasing in Cr:ZnSe and Cr:ZnS waveguides shows the Cr²⁺ gain is kept (core is unirradiated polycrystal).
best_loss: 0.62 dB/cm at 1030 nm (ZnS depressed cladding, ntnu2018zns, conference); ZnSe: 0.5 dB/cm at 800 nm (Heriot-Watt PHOTONICS 2010 conference) and 1.07 dB/cm at 1550 nm (macdonald2010znse)
dlw_notes: Polycrystalline material (grain boundaries). A University of Dayton thesis reports ULI waveguide devices scaled to >5 W (Cr:ZnSe) and >1 W (Fe:ZnSe). Mid-IR guiding at ≈4 µm shown in ZnS (1.1 dB/cm TE).

Caveat: polycrystalline CVD material (grain boundaries in the writing path), and ZnSe absorbs in the blue, so 1025 nm writing is multiphoton with unknown thresholds.

label: Fluoride crystals
name: Fluoride crystals: CaF₂, BaF₂, LiF, LiYF₄ (YLF) / LiLuF₄ (LLF), undoped or rare-earth doped
class_note: Low-index (≈1.39–1.45), wide-window crystals: LiF 0.12–6 µm, BaF₂ 0.15–12 µm (Crystran), CaF₂ ≈0.13–9 µm. Undoped crystals are passive; rare-earth-doped CaF₂ and LiYF₄/LiLuF₄ are laser hosts (waveguide lasers at 574 nm to 1.06 µm in the papers here).
composition: Cubic alkaline-earth / alkali fluorides (CaF₂, BaF₂, LiF) and rare-earth-doped LiYF₄ / LiLuF₄ hosts (Pr, Dy/Tb, Nd/Gd, Yb dopants in the papers). Korth Kristalle grows MgF₂, CaF₂, SrF₂, BaF₂, LiF, NaF.
index_change: fs writing lowers the index in CaF₂ (patent example: ≈−0.012), so the core cannot be the focus. Working geometries: double-track (stress-guided) waveguides in undoped CaF₂ (Gebremichael 2020; also track pairs in Pr:LiYF₄) and depressed cladding (Nd,Gd:CaF₂; Dy,Tb:LiLuF₄; helical cladding in Pr:LLF). Gain survives in the guiding region: waveguide lasing in Yb:CaF₂, Nd,Gd:CaF₂, Pr:LiYF₄ and Dy,Tb:LiLuF₄.
typical_delta_n: ≈ −1×10⁻² in the cladding (CaF₂, patent expectation at 0.5 µJ, not a measured device value; https://image-ppubs.uspto.gov/dirsearch-public/print/downloadPdf/7132223)
writing_regime: Both regimes worked: low-rate athermal writing (Dy,Tb:LiLuF₄: 800 nm, 60 fs, 5 kHz, 92 nJ, 40× objective) and MHz-rate writing with a radially polarized vortex beam (Yb:CaF₂).
best_loss: 0.07 dB/cm (Dy,Tb:LiLuF₄ depressed cladding, baiocco2025dytbllf; test wavelength not quoted); 0.85 dB/cm in Yb:CaF₂ (liu2023ybcaf2)
dlw_notes: No fs-written waveguide paper in BaF₂ or LiF was found. A 2022 Chin. Opt. Lett. paper reports ≈0.12 dB/cm multimode loss in a helical depressed-cladding Pr:LiLuF₄ waveguide (bibliographic data incomplete, not listed). Crystran notes BaF₂ is susceptible to thermal shock.

Caveat: Δn is negative, so the core must sit inside a cladding or between double tracks, and our setup has no vortex/radial-polarisation optics.

label: Si / Ge
name: Crystalline silicon and germanium (inside-bulk writing, IR)
class_note: Semiconductors opaque below their band gap: Si transmits from 1.2 µm (Crystran; gap ≈1.1 eV) to 15 µm with n ≈ 3.42; Ge from 1.5 to 22 µm (Crylink). Writing inside them needs wavelengths beyond the gap: 2.4 µm (Nejadmalayeri 2005), 1.5–1.55 µm (Pavlov 2017, Alberucci 2020). Our CARBIDE at 1025 nm lies below Si's 1.2 µm transmission edge, so it cannot write inside Si or Ge without wavelength conversion.
composition: Single-crystal Si: Czochralski (CZ) material contains oxygen (absorption band at 9 µm), float-zone (FZ) avoids it (Crystran). Germanium: single crystal, m3m, 5.3267 g/cm³ (Crylink).
index_change: Si, fs at 1.5–1.55 µm: positive Δn in the focus (Type I-like core), 3.5–6×10⁻⁴ (Pavlov 2017) up to ≈4×10⁻³ (Alberucci 2020). Si, 2.4 µm fs at 1 kHz: buried single-mode guides at 1.32/1.55 µm, TM-only guiding. Si, ns pulses: index depression ≈−2×10⁻⁴ → tube-shaped depressed cladding (Turnalı 2019). Germanium: no bulk-written waveguide paper found.
writing_regime: High repetition rate helps: at 250 kHz, heat accumulation gives thermal lensing that counteracts plasma defocusing and lets the focus reach deep inside Si (Pavlov 2017). 1 kHz worked at 2.4 µm with a reflective objective (Nejadmalayeri 2005). With 860 fs at 1.55 µm, Δn and shape saturate above 100 nJ (Alberucci 2020).
best_loss: ≤1.2 dB/cm (upper limit) across the telecom band (nejadmalayeri2005si)
dlw_notes: Writing wavelengths used: 2.4 µm (or 2.6 µm, conflicting summaries), 1.5 µm, 1.55 µm — all above the 1.1 µm limit. Writing deep inside Si is limited by plasma defocusing and nonlinear absorption before the focus. Polarization-dependent guiding reported (2005).
our_laser: Not possible with CARBIDE: 1025 nm is absorbed by both crystals (Si transmits only from ≈1.2 µm, Ge from 1.8 µm; Ge band gap 0.67 eV), so the pulse is absorbed near the entrance surface and cannot be focused inside to write a waveguide. All bulk Si waveguides used sub-band-gap light: 2.4 µm at 1 kHz, 1.7 µJ (Nejadmalayeri 2005), 1.5 µm at 250 kHz, 350 fs, 2 µJ (Pavlov 2017), 1.55 µm at 860 fs (Alberucci 2020), or ns pulses (Turnalı 2019); no bulk Ge waveguide paper was found. Writing in Si/Ge would need a ≥1.5 µm source (e.g. Er fibre laser or OPA).
open_questions: Germanium: no fs bulk-written waveguide paper found. Nejadmalayeri 2005 writing wavelength: 2.4 µm vs 2.6 µm in two summaries; pulse duration not quoted. Propagation loss of the Pavlov 2017 and Alberucci 2020 guides not quoted; a sub-ps 1552 nm study reported 'below 3 dB/mm'.
index_change_full: Si, fs at 1.5–1.55 µm: positive Δn in the focus (Type I-like core), 3.5–6×10⁻⁴ (Pavlov 2017) up to ≈4×10⁻³ (Alberucci 2020). Crystallinity of the modified region not stated in the retrieved texts. Germanium: no bulk-written waveguide paper found.

label: PMMA
name: Poly(methyl methacrylate), PMMA (acrylic glass; cast sheet, e.g. PLEXIGLAS GS; clinical-grade PMMA)
class_note: Amorphous, centrosymmetric polymer: no χ(2), no gain. Used for low-cost, biocompatible and flexible photonics (lab-on-chip, polymer optical circuits). Transparent in the visible (92 % for 0F00 sheet)
trade_names: PLEXIGLAS GS (cast acrylic), clear 0F00 (Röhm GmbH (formerly Evonik), Darmstadt), clinical-grade (undoped) PMMA (not stated in results (used by Baum et al. 2007))
composition: Amorphous thermoplastic poly(methyl methacrylate). Cast sheet (PLEXIGLAS GS) and extruded sheet (XT) are separate product lines; the papers used undoped / clinical-grade PMMA (Baum 2007) or commercial bulk PMMA (Zoubir 2004: 12 mm thick sample). Additives (UV absorbers) are grade-specific: GS 0F00 is described as largely UV-absorbing.
index_change: Both signs occur. (1) Type I-like: at sub-ablation fluence the focal volume gets a POSITIVE Δn that can guide directly — Baum 2007 wrote waveguides in undoped clinical-grade PMMA with Δn_max = 4×10⁻³ in the focal region at 387 nm; Scully 2003 wrote index gratings (~5×10⁻⁴) at 800 nm / 1 kHz / 40 fs. (2) Mixed-sign / tubular: Zoubir 2004 (25 MHz oscillator, longitudinal writing) produced 25 µm tubular structures whose dark centre and bright ring have opposite-sign Δn; the guide is the ring region (multimode). (3) 'Cascaded focus' (Pätzold 2016): the focal modification itself does not guide; a refocusing effect writes a positive-Δn zone directly BELOW it, and that zone carries a nearly symmetric fundamental mode (0.5 dB/cm). Double-line stress guides or depressed claddings in bulk PMMA were not found. PMMA is amorphous: no χ(2), gain or crystallinity to preserve.
writing_regime: Published routes range from 1 kHz amplifiers (Scully 2003, 800 nm, 40 fs) through UV/second-harmonic (387 nm) writing (Baum 2007/2010) to a 25 MHz, 20 nJ, 30 fs oscillator with 20 mm/s longitudinal scanning (Zoubir 2004). Pätzold 2016 states that the repetition rate plays a crucial role for the refocusing effect that makes their low-loss guides. Baum 2008: at 800 nm shorter pulses (<100 fs) modify more efficiently; at 387 nm longer (180 fs) pulses are better; incubation with repeated low-fluence pulses reduces bulk damage. At MHz rates heat accumulation melts PMMA — Volpe et al., Opt. Express 23(4), 4114 (2015) used 1030 nm, 650 fs MHz pulses to WELD PMMA layers. Relevance for our CARBIDE (60–1008 kHz): polymers soften at ~70–140 °C (PMMA service temperature ~70 °C, COC Tg 134–142 °C) instead of >500 °C for glasses, and conduct heat poorly. Our inference (not from a paper): heat from successive pulses accumulates at lower repetition rates than in glass and drives the polymer past its softening/decomposition point, giving melting, bubbles or carbonisation instead of a smooth index change. Start at the lowest repetition rate (60–100 kHz), low pulse energy (tens of nJ) and fast scanning, raise the dose by repeated passes rather than by repetition rate, and treat ≥500 kHz as a regime for welding (cf. MHz PMMA welding by heat accumulation) rather than for low-loss guides unless a paper shows otherwise.
best_loss: ≈0.5 dB/cm — patzold2016cascaded
dlw_notes: Writing at 1025 nm (our laser) would need ≥3-photon absorption (our inference from 3PA at 800 nm, Baum 2008; not measured). Mode symmetry: Sowa 2006 ('Symmetric waveguides in PMMA', Opt. Parallel SLM writing (16 beams, 775 nm, 170 fs) in clinical-grade PMMA was used for thick volume phase gratings (Appl. Phys. B 2010, s00340-010-4205-5). Two-photon polymerisation of acrylate resists is a different method (additive, not modification of bulk PMMA) and is not covered here.

label: COC / COP (Topas)
name: Cyclic olefin copolymer / cyclo-olefin polymer (COC: TOPAS; COP: ZEONEX / ZEONOR)
class_note: Amorphous polyolefin, no χ(2) or gain. Chosen over PMMA for higher Tg (134–142 °C for TOPAS grades vs ≈70 °C service temperature of PLEXIGLAS GS), very low water uptake and good C-band usability: fs-written COC waveguides guide at 1550 nm with 2.2 dB/cm (Kefer 2024).
trade_names: TOPAS COC 6013M-07 (TOPAS Advanced Polymers (Polyplastics), Raunheim, Germany), TOPAS COC 5013S-04 / 5013L-10 (TOPAS Advanced Polymers), ZEONEX 480R (COP) (Zeon Corporation (Japan))
composition: Amorphous cyclic-olefin copolymer (COC, TOPAS) or cyclo-olefin polymer (COP, ZEONEX/ZEONOR); glass-clear, high-purity grades. Tg is grade-dependent (134–142 °C for the TOPAS grades seen).
index_change: POSITIVE Δn in the focus (Roth 2020: 'refractive index increase can be achieved inside the substrate' by nonlinear absorption of focused, spatially modulated 514 nm, 450 fs light). Two geometries: (1) single-track Type I core written with SLM beam shaping (Roth 2020, ≤3.2 dB/cm); (2) 'lattice-like' waveguides — a hexagonal array of positive-Δn lines forms the guiding region, so the mode size is set by the lattice (Kefer 2023/2024; single-mode at 1550 nm, 2.2 dB/cm). Bragg gratings are written into the same guides in one step. No depressed-cladding or double-line work found. Amorphous: no χ(2)/gain/crystallinity issues.
writing_regime: Hellmann group (TH Aschaffenburg, Germany) writes at 514 nm with 450 fs pulses and in-situ SLM beam shaping. 514 nm is presumably the second harmonic of a ~1028 nm Yb laser (our inference) — i.e. our CARBIDE would need a harmonic module to copy the recipe; no COC writing at the 1 µm fundamental was found. Start at the lowest repetition rate (60–100 kHz), low pulse energy (tens of nJ) and fast scanning, raise the dose by repeated passes rather than by repetition rate, and treat ≥500 kHz as a regime for welding (cf. MHz PMMA welding by heat accumulation) rather than for low-loss guides unless a paper shows otherwise.

Applications are sensors: relative pressure sensor with a micromilled 300 µm diaphragm, up to 38 pm/kPa over −60…100 kPa (Kefer 2024). UV-fs ablation of COC (Bischoff et al., Polymers 14, 2962, 2022) is surface machining, not waveguide writing. label: PDMS (silicone)
name: Polydimethylsiloxane, PDMS (silicone elastomer, e.g. Dow SYLGARD 184), neat or photosensitised
class_note: Elastomer, amorphous, no χ(2) or gain. Interest is mechanical (flexible, stretchable, biocompatible waveguides, implants, endoscopes) and microfluidic. Lower index (1.41) than PMMA/COC, low thermal conductivity (0.2 W/(m·K), ~6× below fused silica).
composition: Crosslinked polydimethylsiloxane, two-part (base + curing agent) elastomer. For fs writing it is often photosensitised: organic photoinitiators (irgacure-184, benzophenone), germanium compounds, or phenylacetylene diffused into the cured PDMS (Boisvert 2022 and works cited there).
index_change: Type I POSITIVE Δn in the focus, guiding core directly — weak in neat PDMS (~10⁻³), strong when photosensitised (~10⁻², Boisvert 2022). The 2023 review (Chen et al.) describes the Type-I route as: cure PDMS, soak it in a photosensitised monomer, then laser-write; it also shows Type-II (damage-type) modifications separately. No double-line or depressed-cladding PDMS work found. Amorphous, no χ(2)/gain.
typical_delta_n: ≈1×10⁻³ (neat) to ~1×10⁻² (photosensitised, Boisvert 2022); ≈0.06 with phenylacetylene (cited in Boisvert 2022)
writing_regime: Boisvert 2022 mapped Δn against repetition rate 101–606 kHz, writing speed 1–40 mm/s and 1–8 passes — this window overlaps our CARBIDE (60–1008 kHz) directly, so it is the closest published recipe for our laser among the polymers. Relevance for our CARBIDE (60–1008 kHz): polymers soften at ~70–140 °C (PMMA service temperature ~70 °C, COC Tg 134–142 °C) instead of >500 °C for glasses, and conduct heat poorly. Our inference (not from a paper): heat from successive pulses accumulates at lower repetition rates than in glass and drives the polymer past its softening/decomposition point, giving melting, bubbles or carbonisation instead of a smooth index change. Start at the lowest repetition rate (60–100 kHz), low pulse energy (tens of nJ) and fast scanning, raise the dose by repeated passes rather than by repetition rate, and treat ≥500 kHz as a regime for welding (cf. MHz PMMA welding by heat accumulation) rather than for low-loss guides unless a paper shows otherwise.
best_loss: 0.03 dB/cm at 650–700 nm was reported for fs two-photon polymerisation of phenylacetylene inside PDMS (Opt. Mater. Express, doi 10.1364/OME.9.000128, EPFL) — a 2PP-type method, see notes.
dlw_notes: 2PP note: EPFL (Psaltis/Moser labs per news coverage; author list conflicting between sources) wrote ~1.3 µm wide flexible waveguides by photoinitiator-free two-photon polymerisation of phenylacetylene diffused into a PDMS slab with a 680 nm Ti:sapphire laser, 0.03 dB/cm at 650–700 nm (Laser Focus World; Optica newsroom Dec 2018). This is polymerisation of an infused monomer, not modification of PDMS itself, so it is not listed as a paper. Soft material: sample mounting, depth calibration and surface flatness differ from glass; the index change of phenylacetylene-loaded PDMS fades under ambient light.
our_laser: Closest to our laser among the polymers: Boisvert 2022 mapped Δn in photosensitised PDMS over 101–606 kHz, 1–40 mm/s and 1–8 passes (Δn ~1e-2 with irgacure-184 or benzophenone, strongest with benzophenone + Ge), a window entirely inside our 60–1008 kHz; its wavelength, pulse duration, energy and NA were not retrieved, so it is not confirmed as a 1 µm Yb recipe. Expect type I positive Δn mainly after photosensitisation (neat PDMS ~1e-3), with energy to be found by a new scan.

label: Hydrogels (other)
name: Other polymers: silicone and non-silicone hydrogels (contact-lens materials, e.g. Balafilcon A)
class_note: Hydrated, amorphous polymer networks; no χ(2) or gain. Interest is biomedical (index shaping in contact lenses and cornea — 'IRIS', Knox group), not integrated photonics. The fs-induced Δn (+0.06) is far larger than in glasses.
trade_names: Balafilcon A (silicone hydrogel contact-lens material) (not stated in results (Bausch & Lomb co-authors on the Knox-group papers))
composition: Water-containing crosslinked polymer networks. Balafilcon A: silicone hydrogel, ~36 wt% water (secondary: Knox-group patents).
index_change: Type I POSITIVE Δn in the focus, guiding core directly; +0.06 in Balafilcon A at 1.3 nJ (below optical breakdown), lines ~1 µm wide and ~3 µm deep; Raman spectra of written regions almost identical to untreated hydrogel (no large chemical change). Waveguides written inside water-containing hydrogels guide strongly but with high loss from surface roughness (Ding 2008). No χ(2)/gain/crystallinity.
typical_delta_n: up to +0.06 (hydrogels and ocular tissue), up to +0.08 in dye-doped hydrogels (Knox group)
writing_regime: Knox group: tightly focused Ti:sapphire OSCILLATOR pulses (MHz rate, ~1 nJ) — non-amplified, high-NA writing; Our CARBIDE minimum pulse energy and kHz–MHz range are compatible in principle, but the material must stay hydrated (water immersion) and is not a typical photonics substrate. MHz PMMA welding by heat accumulation) rather than for low-loss guides unless a paper shows otherwise.
dlw_notes: Index measured from diffraction efficiencies of written gratings (Ding 2006). Coupling with a tapered lensed fibre while the sample sits in water (Ding 2008). Polystyrene, CYTOP (fluoropolymer; fs work exists mainly as gratings in CYTOP fibres, not searched) and bulk ORMOCER: no fs-written bulk waveguide paper found — not included. Two-photon polymerisation of ORMOCER/acrylate resists is a different, additive method.
our_laser: No hydrogel waveguide paper with a Yb laser was found: Ding 2006/2008 used tightly focused, unamplified Ti:sapphire oscillator pulses (rate not retrieved; ~1.3 nJ below breakdown, attribution probable) for Δn up to +0.06 in Balafilcon A, and the guides were lossy because of surface roughness. The CARBIDE runs at ≤1008 kHz and would need heavy attenuation to reach nJ energies (our inference), so energy and speed need a new scan; samples must stay hydrated (Ding 2008 tested the guides in water).
